capabilities.name: 1. Audience segmentation by behaviour (opened / not-opened / clicked / bounced / replied / converted)
capabilities.evidence: repositories/SubscriberRepository.java:24-36 (search filters q + status + listId only); repositories/CampaignRecipientRepository.java:23-24 (countByCampaignIdAndOpenedAtIsNotNull / ...LastClickedAtIsNotNull are COUNTS only), :34-44 (search filters campaignId+status+q); models/Subscriber.java:35 (status SUBSCRIBED|UNSUBSCRIBED|BOUNCED|COMPLAINED), :46-49 (totalSent/totalOpened/totalClicked/lastEngagedAt counters)
capabilities.notes: Bounced/complained/unsubscribed ARE segmentable, via Subscriber.status which SuppressionService.suppress sets (services/SuppressionService.java:44-46), and GET /api/subscribers?status=BOUNCED exposes it. Opened/clicked exist only as denormalised counters and as aggregate counts; there is NO query anywhere that returns the set of subscribers who opened or did not open a given campaign, and no way to write such a set into a list. Replied and converted have no field, table or code path at all (grep for reply/convert/registration over src/ returns only replyTo and SMTP-reply text). Engagement counters on Subscriber are also lifetime, not per-campaign, so 'opened campaign 3' is unanswerable from them.

capabilities.name: 2. Saved segments / dynamic lists vs static lists
capabilities.evidence: models/MailingList.java:10-26 (fields: id, name, description, kind, createdAt, createdBy - no rule/criteria/filter field); models/ListMember.java:15-34 (plain listId+subscriberId join row); repositories/ListMemberRepository.java:29-36 (countMailable is the only computed view)
capabilities.notes: Every list is static. Membership changes only through explicit writes: CSV import (services/SubscriberService.java:104-111), POST /api/subscribers/add-to-list, POST /api/subscribers/remove-from-list (controllers/AudienceApi.java:183-195). There is no saved-query entity, no re-evaluation job, and MailingList.kind (EVENT|NEWSLETTER|IMPORT|HR|OTHER) is cosmetic - it 'drives the icon and consent copy' per the comment at models/MailingList.java:21.

capabilities.name: 3. Campaign scheduling and send-window / throttle control
capabilities.evidence: services/CampaignService.java:273-291 (@Scheduled(fixedDelay=60_000) runDueCampaigns), :293-310 (schedule/cancelSchedule); models/Campaign.java:33 (scheduledAt); repositories/CampaignRepository.java (findByStatusAndScheduledAtLessThanEqual); services/SesSender.java:69-81 (awaitSendSlot, evenly-spaced slots at maxSendRate); services/CampaignService.java:56 (Semaphore concurrencyGate from aws.ses.maxConcurrency)
capabilities.notes: Scheduling exists: one absolute LocalDateTime per campaign, polled every 60s, so effective granularity is ~1 minute and it fires the whole blast at once. Throttle exists but is PROCESS-WIDE, not per campaign: aws.ses.maxSendRate=12/s (application.properties:46) and aws.ses.maxConcurrency=16 (:47) are shared by campaigns and transactional mail. MISSING: send windows / quiet hours / recipient timezone, per-campaign rate override, batch or drip pacing, pause-and-resume (Campaign.status documents PAUSED at models/Campaign.java:29 but nothing ever sets it), and cross-process locking - runDueCampaigns has no scheduler lock, so two app instances would both fire the same campaign.

capabilities.name: 4. A/B split assignment (deterministic bucketing, variant tracking, winner selection)
capabilities.evidence: No match for variant|abtest|split test|bucket|winner in src/**/*.java (only OpenClassification 'buckets' and String.split). models/Campaign.java:14-46 has one subject and one htmlBody; models/CampaignRecipient.java:21-56 has no variant column; migrate-v2.sql:66-91 creates no variant table
capabilities.notes: Nothing exists. A campaign is one subject + one body + one list. The only way to run an A/B today is to hand-build two campaigns pointed at two hand-split lists, and then the analytics compare is per-campaign (AnalyticsService.byCampaign) rather than per-variant-within-cohort, so cohort x variant cross-tabs are impossible.

capabilities.name: 5. Open tracking + Apple MPP / bot handling (OpenClassifier)
capabilities.evidence: services/SesSender.java:201-206 (1x1 pixel appended before </body> when trackOpens); controllers/TrackingController.java:55-67 (GET /api/mailer/open, no-store headers); analytics/OpenTrackingService.java:59-69 (recordOpen -> classify -> save TrackingEvent -> only HUMAN calls campaigns.trackOpen); analytics/OpenClassifier.java:115-165 (classifyOpen); analytics/OpenClassification.java:13-32 (HUMAN|APPLE_MPP|PROXY|BOT, countsAsEngagement() == HUMAN only)
capabilities.notes: This is the strongest part of the platform. MPP handling: bare AppleWebKit UA with no Version//Safari//Chrome tail is treated as MPP (OpenClassifier.java:222-227), corroborated by Apple network 17.0.0.0/8 (:80) plus optional analytics.appleNetworks CIDRs. Gmail/Yahoo image proxies count as HUMAN unless the fetch lands inside analytics.prefetchWindowSeconds (default 3), because the proxy fetches on render (:140-151). ~80 scanner/crawler/unfurler UA tokens (:33-64). Raw userAgent/ip/secondsSinceSent are persisted (analytics/TrackingEvent.java:45-62) so OpenTrackingService.reclassify (:124-162) can re-run verdicts over history; exposed as POST /api/analytics/reclassify. Known limitation stated in code at OpenTrackingService.java:118-122: legacy openedAt/openCount on CampaignRecipient are NOT retro-corrected.

capabilities.name: 6. Click tracking + per-link attribution
capabilities.evidence: services/SesSender.java:162-180 (rewrites every http(s) href and {{TRACK:url}} to /api/mailer/click?token=..&url=..), :246-250 (trackedUrl); controllers/TrackingController.java:34-53 (scheme allowlist blocks the open-redirect, then redirects regardless of verdict); analytics/OpenTrackingService.java:76-89 (recordClick, classifyClick, HUMAN-only counting); models/ClickEvent.java:10-32; analytics/TrackingEventRepository.java:70-91 (topLinks group by url with unique counts); services/CampaignService.java:389-395 (linkBreakdown)
capabilities.notes: Per-link attribution is by destination URL string, grouped and ranked by unique clickers - GET /api/analytics/links and the 'links' key of GET /api/campaigns/{id}. Two writes happen per human click: a ClickEvent row (legacy path, CampaignService.trackClick:333-347) and a TrackingEvent row (classified path). There are no link IDs or link labels, so two buttons pointing at the same URL are indistinguishable, and adding a UTM per variant would be the only way to separate them. Clicks inside the prefetch window, or from a scanner UA, are recorded as BOT and excluded from every rate (OpenClassifier.java:171-198).

capabilities.name: 7. Reply detection (match replies to a campaign)
capabilities.evidence: mail/MailService.java:128-135 (listMessages by folder), :143-147 (search with Stalwart 'text' filter over subject/addresses/body), :117 folderByRole('inbox'), :189 getMessage; mail/MessageSummary.java (carries threadId and an 'answered' flag); webmail/MailApiController.java:45,125,142 (GET /api/mail/messages, GET /api/mail/search); webmail/MailboxAccess.java:62-100 (mailbox must be unlocked per HTTP session with its password)
capabilities.notes: The inbox CAN be read - JMAP Email/query + Email/get through Stalwart on loopback. But nothing connects it to campaigns: no In-Reply-To or References header is captured (mail/MessageSummary.java has no such field), CampaignRecipient stores messageId from SES (models/CampaignRecipient.java:55) but nothing ever searches on it, there is no REPLIED status, no scheduled scanner, and no campaign_reply table. Structural blocker for automation: MailboxAccess holds the mailbox secret in the browser HttpSession (webmail/MailboxAccess.java:29-33, SESSION_KEY), so a background job has no credential to read the inbox with unless a human has a session open.

capabilities.name: 8. Conversion / registration tracking
capabilities.evidence: controllers/TrackingController.java:84-87 (GET /api/mailer/success returns a static 'Thanks for registering' HTML page and records NOTHING - no token parameter, no repository call); no conversion entity in models/; AnalyticsService.summary (analytics/AnalyticsService.java:53-121) emits no conversion key
capabilities.notes: The success page is decoration. The closest available proxy today is a click on the registration link, visible in ClickEvent/TrackingEvent by URL, which measures intent not completion. There is also no inbound API for a registration system to post back: controllers/PublicApiV1.java:41-74 exposes only /transactional/send, /templates and /ping under API-key auth.

capabilities.name: 9. Bounce + complaint handling and automatic suppression
capabilities.evidence: services/SuppressionService.java:89-114 (@Scheduled(fixedDelay=900_000) syncFromSes mirrors SES's account-level ListSuppressedDestinations), :40-48 (suppress writes global_suppression + flips Subscriber.status + skipPendingForEmail); sns/SnsWebhookController.java:99-124 (Bounce -> suppress only if bounceType==Permanent; Complaint -> always suppress); repositories/CampaignRecipientRepository.java:53-72 (queueFromList excludes suppressed and UNDELIVERABLE-verified addresses)
capabilities.notes: Marked partial because the SNS path is inert as configured: SnsMessageVerifier requires jarurat.sns.allowed-topic-arns and throws 'No SNS topic is configured, so nothing can be accepted' when it is empty (sns/SnsMessageVerifier.java:73-103), and that property is absent from application.properties - every POST /api/sns/ses-events therefore 403s today. The live path is the 15-minute SES suppression-list poll, which is authoritative but delayed and account-level, so bounces are attributed to a campaign only by the email+timestamp heuristic in analytics/AnalyticsAggregateRepository.java:64-83 (documented as over-counting when two campaigns mailed the address). aws.ses.configurationSet is also blank by default (application.properties:45), which SesSender.java:139-147 notes means SES publishes no per-message events at all.

capabilities.name: 10. Unsubscribe + global suppression
capabilities.evidence: models/GlobalSuppression.java:6-20 (email PK, reason UNSUBSCRIBED|BOUNCE|COMPLAINT|MANUAL); services/SesSender.java:117-127 (List-Unsubscribe + List-Unsubscribe-Post one-click headers), :181-193 (honours {{UNSUBSCRIBE_LINK}} or force-appends a footer); controllers/TrackingController.java:69-82 (GET and POST /api/mailer/unsubscribe); services/SuppressionService.java:58-69 (unsubscribeByToken, per-recipient token then legacy subscriber token); controllers/AudienceApi.java:227-256 (list / add / remove suppressions)
capabilities.notes: Complete and enforced at three points: queue time (queueFromList's NOT EXISTS on global_suppression), send time (CampaignService.sendOne:183-190 re-checks and marks SKIPPED), and suppression time (skipPendingForEmail flips in-flight PENDING rows to SKIPPED). Marketing mail cannot be sent without an unsubscribe link - the footer is injected unconditionally when the token is absent.

capabilities.name: 11. Multi-step automation / journeys / triggered sends
capabilities.evidence: services/CampaignService.java:273-291 is the only @Scheduled sender and it only fires campaigns whose single scheduledAt has passed; models/Campaign.java has no parent/next/step/delay field; no journey, step, workflow or trigger class exists in src/
capabilities.notes: Every campaign is a one-shot blast. There is no follow-up, no wait step, no branch on behaviour, no entry trigger. The only sequencing available today is a human creating campaign N+1 by hand, hand-building its audience list, and scheduling it. Transactional sends (controllers/PublicApiV1.java:41) are triggered but only by an external caller, and they are unrelated to campaigns - no tracking, no recipient row, logged separately in transactional_log.

capabilities.name: 12. Templates + merge / personalisation tokens
capabilities.evidence: services/SesSender.java:33 MERGE_TAG = \{\{\s*([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*\}\}, :214-231 applyMergeFields (case-insensitive, HTML-escaped, unresolved tags blanked, UNSUBSCRIBE_LINK and TRACK passed through); services/CampaignService.java:192-195 (merge map for campaigns: NAME, EMAIL, FIRST_NAME only); campaignsplus/TemplateLibraryService.java:43 CAMPAIGN_FIELDS = {NAME, FIRST_NAME, EMAIL}, :84-100 mergeFieldsOf, :157-232 validate; models/EmailTemplate.java:12-52 (MARKETING|TRANSACTIONAL, slug)
capabilities.notes: Token syntax is {{TOKEN}} (uppercase-normalised, whitespace tolerant), plus two specials: {{UNSUBSCRIBE_LINK}} and {{TRACK:https://...}} (SesSender.java:29). Campaign sends resolve exactly THREE tokens - NAME, FIRST_NAME, EMAIL - even though Subscriber carries phone, company and source; any other token in a campaign body renders as empty string. FIRST_NAME has honorific handling so 'Dr. Akanksha Chichra' greets as 'Dr. Akanksha' (CampaignService.java:417-428). Templates only apply to the whole campaign body (POST /api/campaignsplus/templates/apply); there is no partial/block include. Subject-line merge works for transactional (renderTransactional) but campaign subjects are sent raw - CampaignService.sendOne passes campaign.getSubject() straight to SES at :201 with no merge pass.

capabilities.name: 13. Per-recipient state machine
capabilities.evidence: models/CampaignRecipient.java:38-40 - status is PENDING | SENT | FAILED | SKIPPED, and nothing else. Transitions: PENDING set at insert (repositories/CampaignRecipientRepository.java:58), SENT at CampaignService.java:205, FAILED at :219, SKIPPED at :184 and SuppressionService skipPendingForEmail; FAILED->PENDING via requeueFailed (CampaignRecipientRepository.java:74-78)
capabilities.notes: Engagement is NOT part of the status - it lives in side fields: token (unique per send), sentAt, openedAt, lastClickedAt, openCount, clickCount, failReason, messageId. So there is no DELIVERED, BOUNCED, COMPLAINED, REPLIED or CONVERTED state, and no variant or cohort column. The unique constraint (campaignId, subscriberId) at :15-16 means one row per person per campaign, which also means a campaign cannot re-send to the same person - relevant if a journey stage were modelled as a re-send of one campaign.

capabilities.name: 14. Sending identity, domain, SES config, warm-up, rate limiting
capabilities.evidence: application.properties:36-47 (aws.region ap-south-1, aws.ses.domain jarurat.care, fromEmail admin@jarurat.care, fromName, replyTo, configurationSet default EMPTY, maxSendRate 12, maxConcurrency 16); services/SesSender.java:130-137 (From is always the single configured fromEmail; only the display name and reply-to are per-campaign), :69-81 (rate limiter), :90-107 (4-attempt retry with backoff, no retry on AccountSuspended/MailFromDomainNotVerified/MessageRejected), :277-311 (accountHealth, identityHealth: DKIM + MAIL FROM status)
capabilities.notes: One sending identity for the whole platform. models/Campaign.java:20-21 lets a campaign override fromName and replyTo only - the envelope From address is fixed, so per-cohort or per-variant sender identity is impossible without config changes. NO warm-up: no ramp schedule, no daily cap, no per-domain throttling. The pre-send gate does check SES account health and bounce/complaint history against thresholds (campaignsplus/SafetyCheckService.java:132-134, bounceBlockPct 5.0 / complaintBlockPct 0.5) and blocks the send via assertSafeToSend, called on the caller's thread at CampaignService.java:112 so scheduled blasts are gated too.

capabilities.name: 15. Reporting: what AnalyticsService actually computes
capabilities.evidence: analytics/AnalyticsService.java:53-121 summary, :136-161 dailySeries, :178-197 topLinks, :200-210 clients, :233-267 byCampaign, :274-295 classifierInfo
capabilities.notes: summary(campaignId, days): sent, delivered (=sent-bounced), deliveredRate, failedAllTime, skippedAllTime, reliableOpens (unique HUMAN), reliableOpenHits, mppOpens, botOpens, proxyOpens, openRate (HUMAN/delivered), unfilteredOpens + unfilteredOpenRate + inflationFactor (the deliberate 'here is how wrong the old number was' pair), reliableClicks, reliableClickHits, botClicks, clickRate, clickToOpenRate, bounced/bounceRate, complained/complaintRate, unsubscribed/unsubscribeRate (all 3-decimal), plus bounceDangerLine 2.0 and complaintDangerLine 0.1. dailySeries: zero-filled per-day sent / reliableOpens / mppOpens / botOpens / reliableClicks. topLinks: url, clicks, unique, share. clients: mail-client and device split from HUMAN opens only. byCampaign: the same per-campaign row set. Window capped at 365 days (:22). Every rate is HUMAN-only. NOT computed anywhere: revenue, conversions, replies, per-variant or per-cohort splits, per-segment comparison, time-to-open distribution, engagement recency cohorts. Note two parallel reporting stacks exist: this classified one, and the legacy unclassified CampaignService.stats (services/CampaignService.java:353-387) which still powers GET /api/campaigns and GET /api/overview and reports the inflated openRate from CampaignRecipient.openedAt.

dataModel: Campaign (table campaign): id, name (unique), subject, preheader, fromName, replyTo, htmlBody TEXT, listId (nullable FK to mailing_list), status DRAFT|SCHEDULED|SENDING|SENT|PAUSED|FAILED|CANCELLED, scheduledAt, startedAt, completedAt, createdAt, createdBy, totalRecipients, sentCount, failedCount, trackOpens, trackClicks. isEditable() = DRAFT|SCHEDULED|FAILED. models/Campaign.java

CampaignRecipient (table campaign_recipient): id, campaignId, subscriberId, email, name, status PENDING|SENT|FAILED|SKIPPED, token (UUID, unique - the tracking/unsubscribe identity), sentAt, openedAt, lastClickedAt, openCount, clickCount, failReason (500), messageId (SES). UNIQUE(campaignId, subscriberId); indexes on (campaignId,status) and token. models/CampaignRecipient.java

Subscriber (table subscriber): id, email (unique, lowercased on set), firstName, lastName, phone, company, source, status SUBSCRIBED|UNSUBSCRIBED|BOUNCED|COMPLAINED, unsubscribeToken (unique), createdAt, updatedAt, totalSent, totalOpened, totalClicked, lastEngagedAt. isMailable() = SUBSCRIBED. models/Subscriber.java
MailingList (table mailing_list): id, name (unique), description, kind EVENT|NEWSLETTER|IMPORT|HR|OTHER, createdAt, createdBy. Purely static - no rule/criteria field. models/MailingList.java
ListMember (table list_member): id, listId, subscriberId, addedAt. UNIQUE(listId, subscriberId). models/ListMember.java
GlobalSuppression (table global_suppression): email = PRIMARY KEY, reason UNSUBSCRIBED|BOUNCE|COMPLAINT|MANUAL, timestamp. models/GlobalSuppression.java

TrackingEvent (table tracking_event): id, eventType OPEN|CLICK, classification enum HUMAN|APPLE_MPP|PROXY|BOT, campaignId, subscriberId, recipientId, email, url(1000), userAgent(500), ip(64), client(64), deviceType(32), secondsSinceSent (nullable), reason(200), timestamp. Indexes on campaignId, timestamp, (eventType,classification). analytics/TrackingEvent.java
ClickEvent (table click_event): id, campaignId, subscriberId, email, url(1000), timestamp. Legacy per-click table, written alongside TrackingEvent only for HUMAN clicks. models/ClickEvent.java

EmailTemplate (table email_template): id, name, slug (unique, machine id for the transactional API), subject, htmlBody TEXT, type MARKETING|TRANSACTIONAL, description, createdAt, updatedAt, createdBy. models/EmailTemplate.java

VerificationResult (table verification_result): email = PRIMARY KEY, verdict DELIVERABLE|RISKY|UNDELIVERABLE, reason, syntaxOk, domainOk, mxOk, mailboxOk, disposable, roleAccount, catchAll, mxHost, checkedBy, checkedAt. UNDELIVERABLE rows are excluded by queueFromList. verification/VerificationResult.java

MessageLogEntry (table message_log): id, timestamp, direction, fromEmail, toEmail, subject, messageId, sesMessageId, campaignId, outcome, outcomeAt, serverResponse, reportingMta, latencyMs, actor. One row per recipient per send; retention app.messagelog.retentionDays=60. messagelog/MessageLogEntry.java
TransactionalLog (table transactional_log): id, templateSlug, toEmail, subject, status, messageId, error, sentVia, timestamp. models/TransactionalLog.java
User (table app_user): id, email (unique), passwordHash, fullName, role (enum), active, mustChangePassword, createdAt, lastLoginAt, createdBy, failedLoginAttempts, lockedUntil. models/User.java
ApiKey (table api_key): id, name, keyHash, prefix, createdAt, createdBy, lastUsedAt, revokedAt, useCount. models/ApiKey.java

buildGaps.gap: Variant dimension on the send: deterministic A/B bucketing plus variant-tagged tracking
buildGaps.whyNeeded: There is no variant column anywhere. Today a 7-stage x N-cohort x 2-variant campaign means hand-building 7*N*2 separate campaigns and hand-splitting lists, and the analytics can only compare whole campaigns, never variant-within-cohort.
buildGaps.sketch: New table campaign_variant(id, campaign_id, variant_key CHAR e.g. 'A'/'B', weight INT, subject, html_body, preheader, from_name) + new entity models/CampaignVariant.java + repositories/CampaignVariantRepository. Add columns variant_key VARCHAR(8) and cohort_key VARCHAR(64) to campaign_recipient (models/CampaignRecipient.java) and to tracking_event + click_event so every hit carries them. New class services/VariantAssigner.java: assign(campaignId, subscriberId, List<CampaignVariant>) hashing SHA-256(experimentKey + ':' + subscriberId) and mapping the low 32 bits onto the cumulative weight ladder - keyed on a stable experimentKey (not campaignId) so the SAME subscriber lands in the same arm across all 7 stages. Set variant_key inside CampaignRecipientRepository.queueFromList (make it a second UPDATE pass after the insert, one statement, no per-row loop). In CampaignService.sendOne, resolve subject/html from the recipient's variant instead of campaign.getSubject()/getHtmlBody(). Endpoints: POST /api/campaigns/{id}/variants, GET /api/campaigns/{id}/variants, DELETE /api/campaigns/{id}/variants/{variantId}.

COMPLIANCE - INDIA DPDP ACT 2023 (my knowledge, not read from files; verify with counsel). Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by clear affirmative action, and requested with an itemised notice stating the purposes and the data. No pre-ticked boxes, no bundling marketing consent with service consent. The notice must be offered in English or any of the Eighth Schedule languages - given HOPE Circle already ships EN/HI/MR, the email consent notice should match. Data principals have rights to access, correction, erasure and grievance redressal, and the withdrawal of consent must be as easy as giving it (so a one-click unsubscribe, not a login-required preference centre). A named Data Protection Officer or contact for grievances must be published. Health data of cancer patients is not given a separate special category by DPDP (unlike GDPR) but purpose limitation and storage limitation still bite; the Patient Navigator already implements a 3-year retention computed at consent (patients.consent_given / consent_date / consent_method, data_retention_until = consent_date + 3 years, audit_log via triggers, per Patient Navigator/CLAUDE.md), so the mailing list should inherit the same retention discipline rather than keep addresses forever. Children under 18 require verifiable parental consent and no behavioural tracking or targeted advertising - relevant if any paediatric or young-caregiver segment exists.

COMPLIANCE - FOREIGN RECIPIENTS (my knowledge, flagged). Any US recipients (Horizon faculty and attendees from Roswell Park, MD Anderson, Princess Margaret imply US and Canadian addresses) bring CAN-SPAM: accurate From/Reply-To and routing, non-deceptive subject line, identification as an advertisement where applicable, a valid physical postal address in every message, a working opt-out honoured within 10 business days, and liability that cannot be delegated away. Canada brings CASL, which is stricter and is the binding constraint: express or documented implied consent BEFORE sending (implied consent from a conspicuously published business address is limited and message must be relevant to their role), sender identification plus mailing address, an unsubscribe mechanism valid for at least 60 days and honoured within 10 business days, and personal liability for directors with penalties up to CAD 10M. Practical rule: do not send the scraped-list nurture flow to any .ca address or any recipient you cannot evidence consent for. EU/UK recipients bring GDPR/PECR (health-adjacent processing, lawful basis, DPO, transfer mechanism out of India). The mailer already emits List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click headers (mailer/JCF-Mailer/src/main/java/com/jarurat/mailer/services/SesSender.java lines ~119-126), which satisfies the Gmail/Yahoo 2024 bulk-sender requirement; MAILER_PLAYBOOK.md sets the internal complaint target at <0.1%, stricter than the 0.3% Gmail threshold - hold to the internal number.

COMPLIANCE - MEDICAL COMMUNICATION ETHICS, DOCTORS vs PATIENTS (partly my knowledge, flagged). Mailing doctors: under the NMC Professional Conduct regulations Indian physicians face restrictions on accepting gifts, hospitality, travel and honoraria from third parties, and CME must be free of commercial influence - so a Horizon invitation must state that attendance is free, that there is no fee and no honorarium inducement, and must not offer anything of value beyond the education and the certificate. Do not imply CME credit unless it is actually accredited; "Certificate of Participation" is what the files support and is the honest wording. Do not name-drop faculty in a way that implies their endorsement of Jarurat Care rather than their participation in a session. Doctor emails are B2B-professional in register and may be somewhat colder; patient emails are not. Mailing patients: never send a clinical recommendation, never reference an individual's diagnosis, stage or test result in an email (email is not a secure channel and the household may share the inbox), never use open/click behaviour to infer or segment on health status, and keep the referring-doctor relationship intact - the org's own consent flow already promises health information goes "only to the team caring for you and to the doctor who referred you." Two separate sending identities, two separate suppression lists, and no cross-pollination of a patient address into a doctor campaign.

WHAT A NON-PROFIT MUST NEVER DO IN A CANCER EMAIL (synthesis, flagged): promise or imply a cure, remission, life extension or "hope" as an outcome rather than as community; present an unproven, alternative or off-label therapy; recommend or discourage a specific treatment, hospital or drug; use a patient's story or photograph without written, specific, withdrawable consent, and never a deceased patient's without family consent; use fear or deadline pressure ("before it's too late", "only 3 days left") on patients or caregivers; solicit money from a patient or their caregiver on the patient support list at all - keep donor and patient lists physically separate; imply that donating changes a named individual's clinical outcome; publish or leak the fact that a recipient has cancer to anyone, including via a visible To: line, an unmasked list, or a subject line; auto-continue mailing after a bounce or silence in a way that could reach a bereaved family. Add an operational rule the files do not yet have: a bereavement/pause path so mentors can flag an address as do-not-mail without it looking like an unsubscribe.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B1 Human-Open, No Click
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: At least one tracking_event OPEN with classification='HUMAN' against the stage, and zero HUMAN CLICK rows for the same recipient.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: They read it (or their client rendered it with a real human at the wheel) and did not act. This is an interest-without-motivation cohort: the subject line worked, the offer or the CTA did not.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT r.subscriber_id FROM campaign_recipient r WHERE r.campaign_id=:stage AND r.status='SENT' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tracking_event t WHERE t.recipient_id=r.id AND t.event_type='OPEN' AND t.classification='HUMAN') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tracking_event c WHERE c.recipient_id=r.id AND c.event_type='CLICK' AND c.classification='HUMAN');  -- never use campaign_recipient.openedAt here: OpenTrackingService.java:118-122 states legacy openedAt is not retro-corrected by reclassify and is inflated
behaviouralCohorts.appearsAfterStage: S1 (Save the Date, T-21), evaluated at S1+48h; refreshed after every subsequent stage
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: Do not resend the same email louder. Change the object of the CTA: replace 'Register' with one concrete thing they get (agenda PDF, faculty list, certificate, recording). Their next stage should be shorter, not longer.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B2 Clicked, Not Registered
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: HUMAN CLICK on the registration destination URL, and no conversion record within 72h.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: Highest-intent non-converter in the whole flow. They reached the Zoom registration form and abandoned it. In the June data this is invisible: the platform can prove the click and cannot prove the registration.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT DISTINCT t.subscriber_id FROM tracking_event t WHERE t.campaign_id=:stage AND t.event_type='CLICK' AND t.classification='HUMAN' AND t.url LIKE '%zoom.us/webinar/register%' AND t.subscriber_id NOT IN (SELECT lm.subscriber_id FROM list_member lm JOIN mailing_list ml ON ml.id=lm.list_id WHERE ml.name='reg-2026-XX-registrants');  -- the NOT IN arm is a manual daily re-import of the Zoom registrant CSV. NEEDS: conversion_event table + GET /api/mailer/success?token= capture + POST /api/v1/conversions (buildGaps item 4, effort small). Until that ships, registration is knowable only by CSV reconciliation, never in-platform.
behaviouralCohorts.appearsAfterStage: S2 (Registration Open, T-14) onward, evaluated 72h after each stage
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: This is a friction problem, not a persuasion problem. Send a 40-word email with the direct registration link and nothing else, plus one line naming the drop-off cause (Zoom form length, login wall, timezone confusion). Never put this cohort back into the education track.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B3 Registered / Converted
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: Appears in the Zoom registrant export, or (once built) has a conversion_event row of kind='REGISTRATION'.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: The acquisition goal is met. From this moment they must stop receiving acquisition copy and start receiving logistics copy: calendar file, join link, agenda, speaker prep, T-1 and T-0 reminders.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: Materialise list 'reg-<event>-registrants' from the Zoom registrant CSV daily via POST /api/lists/import, then exclude from every promo stage: campaign N+1 targets a list built as (audience list) MINUS (registrants list). Because MailingList is static (models/MailingList.java has no criteria field), 'MINUS' is a re-import, not a query, so it must be rebuilt before every stage. NEEDS: conversion_event + segment/SegmentResolver (buildGaps items 2 and 4) to make this a live rule instead of a nightly CSV chore.
behaviouralCohorts.appearsAfterStage: Any stage from S1; re-evaluated before every single send, not once
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: Sending 'Register now' to someone who registered is the single most credibility-destroying error in webinar email, and it is the one the June stack already solved (send_emails.py calls /meetings/{id}/registrants and skips them). Do not regress on that when moving to JCF-Mailer. Only ever send the Zoom join link to this cohort.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B4 Replied - Interested
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: Inbound reply whose intent classifies as accept, ask-to-be-added, or forward-request.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: A human wrote back positively. Statistically the rarest and most valuable behaviour in the flow, and today it is completely invisible to the platform.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: NEEDS: campaign_reply table + VERP reply-to. Concretely (buildGaps item 5): set a per-recipient Reply-To of reply+{campaign_recipient.token}@jarurat.care in SesSender.build (the Reply-To slot is already per-message at SesSender.java:148), add campaign_reply(id, campaign_id, recipient_id, subscriber_id, jmap_email_id UNIQUE, subject, received_at, detected_via), and run ReplyScanner @Scheduled over MailService.listMessages. NEEDS: campaign_reply.intent VARCHAR(16) IN (INTERESTED, QUESTION, NOT_NOW, OPT_OUT), set by a human or an LLM pass. NEEDS: a service credential in MailCredentialStore, because MailboxAccess.java:29-33 keeps the mailbox secret in the browser HttpSession, so no background job can read the inbox today.
behaviouralCohorts.appearsAfterStage: S1 onward, within 24h of any stage
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: Automation stops. A person answers, from a person's address, and registers them by hand if needed. This is also the cohort that justifies the campaign brief's peer-to-peer clinician send: a warm reply is the strongest evidence a human relationship exists.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B5 Replied - Question or Objection
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: Reply asking about timing, CME credit, certificate, recording availability, fee, or relevance to their subspecialty.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: Interested but blocked by one missing fact. Different from B4 because the correct next action is an answer, not a registration.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: campaign_reply.intent='QUESTION' (NEEDS, as B4). Interim manual rule: a human reads the partnership@jarurat.care inbox after each stage and adds the address to static list 'replied-question-<event>' via POST /api/subscribers/add-to-list.
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: The answer is usually already in the knowledge base (free, no fee, Certificate of Participation for all registrants, every session recorded and shared, live Q&A). Answer in one sentence and register them in the same reply. Every repeated question is also a copy defect: if three people ask about the certificate, the certificate line is missing from the template.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B6 Replied - Not Now / Defer
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: Reply saying wrong topic, wrong date, on leave, or ask me next time.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: A soft no with an implied yes later. Not an opt-out, and treating it as one loses a warm contact; treating it as interest burns one.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: campaign_reply.intent='NOT_NOW' (NEEDS). Action rule: remove from the current event's audience list (POST /api/subscribers/remove-from-list) and add to 'defer-until-next-horizon'. Do NOT add to global_suppression, because SuppressionService.suppress also flips Subscriber.status and that is effectively irreversible for future campaigns.
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: Zero further emails for this event. Re-entry only at the next edition's S1. This is the cohort where the difference between a list and a relationship shows up.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B7 Replied - Opt Out By Reply
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: Reply saying stop, remove me, unsubscribe, or do not contact.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: An unsubscribe expressed in the only channel the recipient trusts. It has exactly the same legal and ethical weight as clicking the unsubscribe link, and none of the platform's automation catches it.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: POST /api/suppressions/add?email=... immediately (AudienceApi.java:245), which writes global_suppression(reason='MANUAL'), flips Subscriber.status and calls skipPendingForEmail so in-flight PENDING rows go SKIPPED. Target SLA: same working day. NEEDS: campaign_reply.intent='OPT_OUT' to automate; until then this is a named human duty, not a nice-to-have.
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: Highest-severity behavioural signal in the model. A reply-based opt-out that is ignored becomes a spam complaint on the next stage, and complaints are measured against a 0.1% danger line and a 0.5% block threshold (SafetyCheckService complaintBlockPct). One ignored reply on a 3,363 list can cost the sending reputation for the whole series.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B8 Hard Bounced
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: Subscriber.status='BOUNCED' or a global_suppression row with reason='BOUNCE'.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: The address does not exist. Permanent, immediate, non-negotiable removal.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT s.id FROM subscriber s WHERE s.status='BOUNCED' OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM global_suppression g WHERE g.email=s.email AND g.reason='BOUNCE');  -- live path today is the 15-minute SES suppression poll (SuppressionService.syncFromSes:89-114), which is account-level and delayed. Per-stage attribution uses the email+timestamp heuristic at AnalyticsAggregateRepository.java:64-83, which the code itself documents as over-counting when two campaigns mailed the same address. NEEDS: jarurat.sns.allowed-topic-arns and aws.ses.configurationSet set, or POST /api/sns/ses-events 403s on every payload and per-message events are never published at all.
behaviouralCohorts.appearsAfterStage: S1+15min at the earliest, realistically S1+1h given the poll interval
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: Not a marketing cohort, a deliverability one. On a 92% free-mail list these are mostly abandoned personal Gmail accounts, and they cluster in the oldest scraped rows. Every hard bounce that survives into stage 2 is a second hit against the same 5.0% bounce block threshold.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B9 Repeated Soft Bounce / Deferred
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: Two or more stages where the send did not land cleanly for the same address: campaign_recipient.status='FAILED' with a retryable fail_reason, or message_log rows with a deferral outcome.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: Mailbox full, greylisted, throttled by the receiving MTA, or reputation-filtered. Looks alive but is quietly not being delivered.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT r.subscriber_id, COUNT(DISTINCT r.campaign_id) AS bad_stages FROM campaign_recipient r WHERE r.status='FAILED' AND r.sent_at > now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY r.subscriber_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.campaign_id) >= 2;  UNION with message_log: SELECT to_email FROM message_log WHERE outcome NOT IN ('DELIVERED','SENT') AND timestamp > now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY to_email HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT campaign_id) >= 2.  HONEST LIMIT: campaign_recipient.FAILED captures SES-side rejects, not post-acceptance soft bounces; true soft bounces arrive only via SNS, which is inert today. message_log retention is app.messagelog.retentionDays=60, so a 7-stage flow is inside the window but a cross-event lookback is not. NEEDS: SNS wired (topic ARN + configurationSet), and NEEDS: campaign_recipient.bounced_at (buildGaps item 7).
behaviouralCohorts.appearsAfterStage: S3 at the earliest, because the rule needs two stages of evidence
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: Suppressing on the first soft bounce throws away good addresses; ignoring it burns reputation on addresses that will never deliver. Two strikes then park for the rest of the flow, retry at the next event, suppress at four.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B10 Complained
behaviouralCohorts.definition: They pressed the spam button. SnsWebhookController suppresses on every complaint regardless of type, and correctly so.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT s.id FROM subscriber s WHERE s.status='COMPLAINED' OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM global_suppression g WHERE g.email=s.email AND g.reason='COMPLAINT'); -- monitor the rate, not just the set: GET /api/analytics/summary returns complaintRate against complaintDangerLine 0.1, and SafetyCheckService blocks the next send above complaintBlockPct 0.5.
behaviouralCohorts.appearsAfterStage: S1 onward, usually concentrated on the first send to cold or scraped provenance
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: Permanent, and diagnostic. Complaints are not evenly distributed: if they concentrate in one pre-send cohort (P6 cold pipeline addresses is the prime suspect), that cohort's provenance is the defect and the fix is to stop mailing it, not to soften the copy.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B11 Machine-Open Only (MPP / Proxy / Bot)
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: Every open event for this person across the flow classifies as APPLE_MPP, PROXY or BOT, and there is not one HUMAN event of any kind.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: The open pixel fired but no human is evidenced. Apple Mail Privacy Protection prefetches images on delivery whether or not the message is ever displayed; security scanners and link unfurlers fetch on receipt; Gmail and Yahoo proxies fetch on render but are treated as PROXY inside the prefetch window.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT r.subscriber_id FROM campaign_recipient r WHERE r.status='SENT' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tracking_event t WHERE t.subscriber_id=r.subscriber_id AND t.classification IN ('APPLE_MPP','PROXY','BOT')) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tracking_event h WHERE h.subscriber_id=r.subscriber_id AND h.classification='HUMAN');  -- classification is already computed by OpenClassifier.java:115-165 and OpenClassification.countsAsEngagement() is HUMAN-only. Raw user_agent/ip/seconds_since_sent are persisted, so POST /api/analytics/reclassify can re-run verdicts if the MPP heuristics are tuned.
behaviouralCohorts.appearsAfterStage: S1+24h, and it is the cohort that grows fastest across stages
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: NEVER treat a machine open as engagement, for four separate reasons. (1) It is not evidence of reading: MPP fires on delivery, so the same person generates an 'open' whether they read it or deleted it unseen. (2) It is a device property, not a person property: MPP incidence correlates with owning an iPhone, so any branch or A/B winner decided on it measures Apple market share, not subject-line quality. (3) It starves conversion: promoting an MPP-only person out of the reminder track removes exactly the send that would have converted them, because the reminder is the one that works. (4) The platform already publishes the size of the lie as inflationFactor and unfilteredOpenRate next to the HUMAN openRate. Correct handling: keep them in the flow, decide their branches on clicks only, and report them in their own line, never inside openRate.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B12 Silent but Delivered (Open-Blind)
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: status='SENT', no bounce, no suppression, and zero tracking_event rows of ANY classification.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: Usually the largest cohort in the flow. Images off, text-only client, corporate gateway stripping the pixel, or genuinely unread. The platform cannot tell these apart.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT r.subscriber_id FROM campaign_recipient r WHERE r.campaign_id=:stage AND r.status='SENT' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tracking_event t WHERE t.recipient_id=r.id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM global_suppression g WHERE g.email=r.email);
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: Zero opens is not zero reads. Decide this cohort on clicks and replies only, and give it the plain-text-flavoured, link-light variant the campaign brief already favours ('Quick note, GI oncology session on 12 June'). If a person in this cohort ever clicks, they were never disengaged and the open data was simply blind to them.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B13 Serial Opener, Never Converts
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: HUMAN opens on three or more distinct stages, zero HUMAN clicks across the entire flow.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: Reliable readers who never act. On a GI-oncology list these are frequently trainees, students and industry watchers who value the content and will not attend a Saturday evening Zoom.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT t.subscriber_id FROM tracking_event t WHERE t.event_type='OPEN' AND t.classification='HUMAN' AND t.campaign_id IN (:stageIds) GROUP BY t.subscriber_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.campaign_id) >= 3 AND t.subscriber_id NOT IN (SELECT c.subscriber_id FROM tracking_event c WHERE c.event_type='CLICK' AND c.classification='HUMAN' AND c.campaign_id IN (:stageIds));
behaviouralCohorts.appearsAfterStage: S4 (T-4) at the earliest, because it needs three stages of open evidence
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: Change the offer, not the pressure. Sell the recording and the Certificate of Participation instead of the live seat, drop them to one email per event, and stop counting them as pipeline. They keep the open rate looking healthy while contributing nothing to registrations, which is precisely how a campaign convinces itself it is working.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B14 Late Engager
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: First HUMAN event for a stage arrives more than 48h after that stage was sent, measured by tracking_event.seconds_since_sent.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: Reads on their own schedule, typically clinicians who clear their inbox at the weekend. Invisible to any 24h decision window.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT t.subscriber_id, MIN(t.seconds_since_sent) AS first_gap FROM tracking_event t WHERE t.campaign_id=:stage AND t.classification='HUMAN' GROUP BY t.subscriber_id HAVING MIN(t.seconds_since_sent) > 172800;  -- seconds_since_sent is already persisted on tracking_event (analytics/TrackingEvent.java:45-62), so this needs no new field
behaviouralCohorts.appearsAfterStage: S2 onward, and it retroactively rewrites the verdict on earlier stages
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: Two operational consequences. First, never judge a stage's performance or call an A/B winner at 24h; on this audience a meaningful share of the response has not happened yet. Second, never demote someone to a sunset cohort for silence measured inside 48h. If a late engager opens S2 after S3 was already sent, S3 targeted them with the wrong branch, which is an argument for pacing stages no tighter than 72h.

behaviouralCohorts.name: B15 Forwarded / Off-List Arrival
behaviouralCohorts.triggerSignal: A registrant or attendee whose email is not in the subscriber table, or a HUMAN click carrying the forward-tagged URL.
behaviouralCohorts.definition: Word of mouth. The measured June reality: of 209 unique attendee addresses on 27 June, only 18 appear on the 3,363-address emailed list. 191 arrived through channels email cannot see.
behaviouralCohorts.sqlOrRule: Path A (measurable today): give the forwardable share link a distinct URL with ?source=forward, then SELECT url, COUNT(DISTINCT subscriber_id) FROM tracking_event WHERE event_type='CLICK' AND classification='HUMAN' AND url LIKE '%source=forward%' GROUP BY url. Per-link attribution is by destination URL string only (no link ids), so a distinct URL is the ONLY way to separate a forward click from a normal one. Path B: reconcile the Zoom registrant export against subscriber.email; the non-matches are the off-list arrivals. NEEDS: consent capture before adding them, since a Zoom registration for one event is not blanket marketing consent under the DPDP framing in the campaign brief.
behaviouralCohorts.appearsAfterStage: S2 onward for clicks; the full picture only after the event
behaviouralCohorts.whyDifferent: This cohort proves whether the email programme is the growth engine or a bystander. On 27 June it was a bystander: 18 of 209 attendees came from the list. Until that ratio moves, optimising subject lines is optimising the wrong variable, and the forwardable asset plus the peer-to-peer clinician send deserve more investment than another reminder stage.

exitRules: PERMANENT, PLATFORM-ENFORCED: unsubscribe. GET or POST /api/mailer/unsubscribe?token= writes global_suppression(reason='UNSUBSCRIBED'), flips Subscriber.status and calls skipPendingForEmail so in-flight PENDING rows become SKIPPED. Enforcement happens at three separate points (queueFromList NOT EXISTS, CampaignService.sendOne re-check at :183-190, and suppression time), and SesSender force-appends an unsubscribe footer when {{UNSUBSCRIBE_LINK}} is absent, so marketing mail literally cannot ship without the exit. Never remove a row from global_suppression to 're-permission' someone.
PERMANENT: spam complaint. SnsWebhookController suppresses on every complaint regardless of type. No win-back, no re-import, no exception for a senior clinician you want at the event.

PERMANENT: hard bounce. Suppressed by SuppressionService via the SES suppression-list poll or, once wired, the Permanent-bounce branch of the SNS handler. Re-importing the same address in a later CSV does not resurrect it, because queueFromList excludes suppressed addresses at queue time.

PERMANENT: verification verdict UNDELIVERABLE. queueFromList already excludes UNDELIVERABLE-verified addresses, so this exit is enforced without any marketer action. Re-verification is allowed only if the address was checked more than 180 days ago.

PERMANENT: opt-out expressed in a reply. Must be actioned by hand via POST /api/suppressions/add?email= on the same working day, with the same finality as a link unsubscribe. NEEDS: campaign_reply.intent='OPT_OUT' to make this automatic instead of a standing human duty.

PERMANENT: domain-level burn. Five or more hard bounces or any complaint concentrated on one recipient domain means suppress the whole domain, per the campaign brief's own rule. NEEDS: domain-level suppression; global_suppression keys on email PK, so today this is a scripted loop of POST /api/suppressions/add over every address at that domain.

EVENT-SCOPED EXIT: registered. Leaves the acquisition flow, enters the logistics flow (calendar, join link, T-1, T-0). Rebuild the target list before every stage, because MailingList is static and a person who registered after the last rebuild will otherwise be told to register again.

EVENT-SCOPED EXIT: replied not-now. Removed from this event's lists, parked on 'defer-until-next-horizon', re-entered only at the next edition's S1. Do NOT write a suppression row for this, since suppression also flips Subscriber.status and is not meant to be undone.

EVENT-SCOPED EXIT: the event happened. Every promo stage is dead the moment the webinar starts; only the thank-you, recording and certificate sends survive, and they go to different cohorts (attended vs registered-no-show) with different copy.

FATIGUE EXIT (sunset): four consecutive stages SENT with zero tracking_event rows of any classification and zero clicks. Move to a quarterly-only list rather than suppressing. Rationale: on a 92% free-mail list, four silent stages is the point where continued sending buys complaints instead of registrations.

FREQUENCY-CAP PARK (temporary, not an exit): more than three sends to one address in any rolling seven days. SELECT to_email FROM message_log WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY to_email HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3, then drop those subscriber ids from the next stage's list before queueing. NEEDS: nothing new, but it must be run manually before each send because there is no journey engine to enforce it.

HARD EXCLUSION (never enters): internal monitoring addresses, JCF staff, the founder's own inbox, and any address on the pipeline SUPPRESS_do_not_send export. Keep them on a named exclusion list and diff every import against it, because the June Postmark script injected an internal monitoring copy into every batch and that pattern silently pollutes every rate you compute.
precedenceRules: RULE 0 - platform absolutes win before marketing logic gets a vote. If global_suppression has the email, or Subscriber.status is not SUBSCRIBED, or verification_result.verdict='UNDELIVERABLE', the person is not in any cohort. This is not a policy choice you can override: queueFromList and CampaignService.sendOne both enforce it independently, so a 'clever' segment that includes these people just produces SKIPPED rows.

RULE 1 - negative outranks positive, always, and severity orders the negatives: COMPLAINED > HARD BOUNCED > OPT-OUT-BY-REPLY > REPEATED SOFT BOUNCE > everything else. A person who opened four stages and then complained is a complainer, not an engaged reader. Never let a positive signal rescue an address from a negative one, no matter how senior the contact.

RULE 2 - explicit human intent outranks every inferred signal. A reply saying 'not now' beats three HUMAN opens. A reply saying 'stop' beats a registration. People telling you what they want is better data than a pixel, and there is no threshold of engagement that overrules a stated preference.

RULE 3 - conversion outranks intent. Registered (B3) beats clicked-not-registered (B2), which beats opened-not-clicked (B1), which beats silent (B12). Assign to the highest rung reached, then send the copy for that rung and no other.

RULE 4 - HUMAN beats machine, and machine never promotes. If a person has any HUMAN event, classify on the HUMAN event and ignore the APPLE_MPP, PROXY and BOT rows. If every event is machine-classified, the person is B11 and is treated as SILENT for every branching decision. A machine open must never move anyone up the ladder in Rule 3, never win an A/B test, and never appear inside a reported open rate. OpenClassification.countsAsEngagement() already encodes this; the cohort model must not quietly re-introduce what the classifier removed.

RULE 5 - behavioural outranks pre-send. A P6 cold pipeline address that clicks is no longer cold; a P1 proven attendee who goes silent for four stages is no longer warm. Provenance sets the starting copy, behaviour sets everything after that. The most common cohort-model failure is a warm label that never expires.

RULE 6 - most recent stage wins on ties. If someone is B1 on S2 and B2 on S3, they are B2. Cohort membership is evaluated per stage against the immediately preceding stage's events, with the whole-flow cohorts (B13 serial opener, B14 late engager) as roll-ups layered on top.

RULE 7 - frequency cap outranks cohort strategy. If a person is due a stage but has already had three sends in seven days, they skip the stage regardless of how good their cohort looks. The cap protects the sending domain, which is a shared asset across every future Horizon edition.

RULE 8 - deliverability tier caps volume, it does not choose copy. A Tier B risky or catch-all address in the same behavioural cohort as a Tier A address gets the same message but fewer stages (S2, S5 and S6 only). Tier and behaviour are independent axes; do not collapse them into one label.

RULE 9 - exactly one cohort_key per person per stage. Resolve the precedence chain top to bottom, take the first match, stop. Overlapping cohorts make reporting uninterpretable and make double-sends inevitable, and the (campaign_id, subscriber_id) unique constraint on campaign_recipient will silently swallow the second attempt rather than warn you.

RULE 10 - snapshot the resolved cohort at queue time, do not recompute it at report time. NEEDS: cohort_key VARCHAR(64) on campaign_recipient, tracking_event and click_event (buildGaps item 1). Without it, a cohort that changes between send and analysis rewrites history and any stage-over-stage comparison is fiction. Until the column exists, the honest workaround is one campaign per cohort per stage, named cohort-first, so campaign_id carries the cohort identity.

RULE 11 - when two rules genuinely tie, prefer the action that sends fewer emails. On a 3,363-address list with one shared sending identity, a bounce block threshold of 5.0% and a complaint block of 0.5%, the cost of one unnecessary send is systemic and the cost of one skipped send is a single missed registration.

preSendCohorts.name: P0 Non-Mailable on Arrival
preSendCohorts.definition: Everyone who is already excluded before the first send: unsubscribed, bounced, complained, manually suppressed, or verified UNDELIVERABLE. This cohort exists on day zero and its correct size is the number you must know before you promise anyone a reach figure.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT s.id, s.email FROM subscriber s LEFT JOIN global_suppression g ON g.email = s.email LEFT JOIN verification_result v ON v.email = s.email WHERE s.status <> 'SUBSCRIBED' OR g.email IS NOT NULL OR v.verdict = 'UNDELIVERABLE';  -- enforced automatically by CampaignRecipientRepository.queueFromList (:53-72) and again by CampaignService.sendOne (:183-190)
preSendCohorts.estShare: Near 0% on JCF-Mailer day one, and that is a trap, not good news. The June sends ran on Postmark, so no bounce, complaint or unsubscribe from those two blasts exists in this database. NEEDS: import of the Postmark suppression and bounce export into global_suppression before the first JCF-Mailer send. Realistic true figure once imported: 4 to 8% of 3,363 (roughly 130 to 270 addresses), based on a 92% free-mail list that has been mailed at least twice.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: They get nothing, ever. Treating a fresh platform as a fresh audience is the single most expensive day-zero mistake available here: it re-mails people who already opted out of the same series through a different vendor, and it lands those complaints against a brand new SES reputation on a domain with zero warm-up.

preSendCohorts.name: P1 Proven Attendee, On List
preSendCohorts.definition: Addresses on the current mailable list that appear in the 27 June Zoom attendee log. They received the email, registered, and showed up. Highest-trust cohort in the entire model.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: Import the attendee log's 'User Email' column into list 'horizon-2026-06-27-attendees' (kind=EVENT) via POST /api/lists/import, then: SELECT s.id FROM subscriber s JOIN list_member lm ON lm.subscriber_id=s.id JOIN mailing_list ml ON ml.id=lm.list_id WHERE ml.name='horizon-2026-06-27-attendees' AND s.status='SUBSCRIBED' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM global_suppression g WHERE g.email=s.email);
preSendCohorts.estShare: MEASURED: 18 of 3,363, which is 0.5%. I counted 209 unique attendee emails in the 27 June log and intersected them with horizon-clean.csv; only 18 matched. This is far smaller than anyone would guess and it is the most important number in this document.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: They need no persuasion, only a date. Two-line email, warm, from a named human, referencing the specific session they attended. They are also the natural seed for the peer-to-peer clinician send and the forwarding ask, because they are the only people with demonstrated willingness to spend a Saturday evening on a Horizon session.

preSendCohorts.name: P2 Proven Attendee, Not On List
preSendCohorts.definition: The 191 unique addresses that attended 27 June but are absent from the emailed list. They arrived through partner promotion, WhatsApp, social or forwards. The single highest-value untapped cohort JCF owns.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: Attendee emails MINUS subscriber.email. Load as a separate list 'attendees-offlist-2026-06-27' with subscriber.source='zoom_attendee_20260627' so provenance survives. Gate before mailing: verify with POST /api/verification/addresses, and record a consent basis, because a Zoom registration for one event is not blanket marketing consent under the DPDP framing in the campaign brief. NEEDS: subscriber.consent_basis and consent_captured_at; today the only carrier is the free-text source field.
preSendCohorts.estShare: MEASURED: 191 addresses, 91% of all 27 June attendees. Adding them grows the mailable warm base by roughly 5.7% of list volume and by an order of magnitude in quality.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: First contact must acknowledge how they arrived ('you joined our 27 June gastric and gastroesophageal session') or it reads as a scrape. Their first email is a permission-and-welcome email, not stage 1 of a promo flow. Never drop them cold into the middle of an existing sequence.

preSendCohorts.name: P3 Registered, Did Not Attend
preSendCohorts.definition: Addresses in a Zoom registrant snapshot with no matching row in the attendee log for that event. Intent proven, attendance not: timing, timezone, or the reminder never reached them.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: Import registrant CSV to list 'reg-snapshot-<event>', attendee CSV to 'attendees-<event>', compute the difference offline (the platform has no set operations because MailingList has no criteria field) and import the result as 'registered-noshow-<event>'. Then target that list directly.
preSendCohorts.estShare: MEASURED but ambiguous: registered_users.csv holds 163 addresses of which 128 are on the emailed list, and only 9 of the 163 appear in the 27 June attendee log. The likeliest reading is that this snapshot belongs to the 12 June pancreatic event, not the 27 June gastric one (the folder is stamped 20 May and the Zoom meeting id in send_emails.py is a placeholder, so I cannot confirm it). Under that reading, 154 of 163 are 12 June registrants who did not attend 27 June, and the 9 overlap is a genuine cross-event repeat cohort. Plan for roughly 3 to 5% of list volume per event.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: Never send this cohort the same 'register now' copy as a cold contact. Lead with the recording and the Certificate of Participation, and ask the one diagnostic question that fixes the next event: was it the time, the topic, or the reminder? A no-show is a solved-intent problem with an unsolved logistics problem.

preSendCohorts.name: P4 Platform-History Engaged
preSendCohorts.definition: Subscribers with real JCF-Mailer engagement history: mailed before, opened before, engaged recently. This is the cohort the data model was built to express.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT id FROM subscriber WHERE status='SUBSCRIBED' AND total_sent >= 1 AND total_opened >= 1 AND last_engaged_at >= now() - interval '180 days';  -- worth knowing: OpenTrackingService only calls campaigns.trackOpen for HUMAN classifications, so total_opened is MPP-clean going forward, unlike the legacy CampaignRecipient.openedAt field
preSendCohorts.estShare: 0% on day one. Every one of these counters is zero because no campaign has ever been sent from this platform. The counters are also lifetime, not per-campaign, so even once populated they can answer 'has ever opened' but never 'opened stage 3'.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: Include it in the architecture now precisely because it is empty now. Naming an empty cohort forces the team to plan how it fills, prevents someone inventing a fake warm segment from list provenance, and makes clear that per-stage truth will always come from tracking_event, never from these counters.

preSendCohorts.name: P5 Mailed Elsewhere, No Platform History
preSendCohorts.definition: The bulk of the list: addresses that received the June Postmark blasts but carry zero evidence of it inside JCF-Mailer. They are warm in reality and cold in the database.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT s.id FROM subscriber s JOIN list_member lm ON lm.subscriber_id=s.id JOIN mailing_list ml ON ml.id=lm.list_id WHERE ml.name='horizon-clean-20260818' AND s.total_sent = 0 AND s.status='SUBSCRIBED';
preSendCohorts.estShare: Roughly 3,150 of 3,363, about 94% of the list, once P0 to P3 are carved out. This is the default cohort and it should be named as such rather than left as the unlabelled remainder.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: Copy must assume prior contact without claiming a relationship ('you may have joined us in June'), and the first JCF-Mailer send to them is effectively a re-permission moment on a brand new sending domain. Send it to the verified slice first, in batches, and watch the bounce and complaint rates against the 5.0% and 0.5% block thresholds before releasing the rest.

preSendCohorts.name: P6 Cold, Never Mailed
preSendCohorts.definition: Net-new addresses from the classification pipeline that have never been contacted by any JCF channel.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT id FROM subscriber WHERE total_sent = 0 AND status='SUBSCRIBED' AND source LIKE 'pipeline_verified_%' AND created_at >= :importDate;  -- provenance stamped into subscriber.source at import time, since the schema has no provenance column of its own
preSendCohorts.estShare: 25 addresses if the audience stays at horizon-clean.csv (the delta versus the older 5000-email file), which is 0.7%. If the team taps the pipeline's 22,023 campaign-ready leads, this cohort instantly becomes 87% of everything mailed and dominates the risk profile.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: Highest complaint risk, lowest conversion, and a completely separate copy job: they need to be told who Jarurat Care Foundation is before they are told about a webinar. Never mix them into the same campaign as P1 to P3, because their bounce and complaint rates will be attributed to the whole send and can trip the pre-send safety gate for everyone. Ramp them slowly and separately: this domain has no warm-up schedule at all (no ramp, no daily cap, no per-domain throttle).

preSendCohorts.name: P7 Deliverability Tier A - Verified Clean
preSendCohorts.definition: Verified DELIVERABLE, not disposable, not a role account, not catch-all. Safe to mail at volume.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT s.id FROM subscriber s JOIN verification_result v ON v.email = s.email WHERE v.verdict='DELIVERABLE' AND v.disposable=false AND v.role_account=false AND v.catch_all=false AND v.checked_at >= now() - interval '180 days' AND s.status='SUBSCRIBED';
preSendCohorts.estShare: Unknown until POST /api/verification/list is run against the imported list, which should be the very first operation on day zero. Expect 70 to 80% on a curated doctor list. Pipeline-wide the ratio was harsher: 86,298 deliverable out of 339,529 processed.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: This tier goes first in every send order, because it establishes the domain's reputation before any risky address touches it. Tier is a volume-and-sequence decision, not a copy decision: do not write different words for Tier A, just send to them first and in larger batches.

preSendCohorts.name: P8 Deliverability Tier B - Risky, Catch-All or Unverified
preSendCohorts.definition: RISKY verdicts, catch-all domains where mailbox existence is unprovable, and addresses never probed at all.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT s.id FROM subscriber s LEFT JOIN verification_result v ON v.email = s.email WHERE s.status='SUBSCRIBED' AND (v.email IS NULL OR v.verdict='RISKY' OR v.catch_all=true OR v.checked_at < now() - interval '180 days');
preSendCohorts.estShare: 15 to 25% of the list is a reasonable planning figure. The pipeline's own export shape supports it: 22,023 verified against 20,823 unverified and 12,998 catch-all.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: Mail them at reduced frequency (S2, S5 and S6 only, never all seven stages) and only after Tier A has sent cleanly. Catch-all domains accept everything at SMTP time and then discard silently, so they inflate the delivered count and depress every rate computed from it. If a Tier B address produces one HUMAN click, promote it to Tier A permanently: a real human is the best verification there is.

preSendCohorts.name: P9 Role and Shared Mailboxes
preSendCohorts.definition: info@, contact@, oncology@, secretary@ style addresses that reach a department or a gatekeeper rather than a named clinician.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT s.id FROM subscriber s JOIN verification_result v ON v.email=s.email WHERE v.role_account = true;  -- fallback without verification data: split_part(s.email,'@',1) IN ('info','contact','admin','office','secretary','oncology','reception','enquiry','department')
preSendCohorts.estShare: 1 to 3% of 3,363, so roughly 35 to 100 addresses. Low, because I measured 92.1% of the list on free-mail consumer domains (gmail, yahoo, hotmail, outlook, rediff and friends). This is a personal-inbox doctor list, not an institutional one.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: Personalisation is actively wrong here. 'Dear Dr. [Last Name]' to info@hospital.org signals a mail merge and gets deleted by the assistant who reads it. Write for a forwarder: name the intended recipient category in the first line, keep it short, and make the forwardable block obvious. These are also the addresses most likely to complain, because nobody personally consented.

preSendCohorts.name: P10 Merge-Unsafe Identity
preSendCohorts.definition: Records where first_name is missing, blank, an honorific only, initials only, or otherwise cannot produce a safe greeting.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: SELECT id FROM subscriber WHERE status='SUBSCRIBED' AND (first_name IS NULL OR btrim(first_name)='' OR length(btrim(first_name)) < 2 OR lower(btrim(first_name)) ~ '^(dr|prof|mr|ms|mrs)\.?$' OR first_name ~ '^[A-Z]\.?([A-Z]\.?)*$');
preSendCohorts.estShare: 12 blank first names are documented in horizon-clean.csv (0.36%), but the real merge-unsafe population is larger once honorific-only, initials-only and ALL-CAPS records are counted: budget 3 to 6%, roughly 100 to 200 addresses.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: This is a data-quality cohort with a direct copy consequence. Campaign sends resolve exactly three tokens (NAME, FIRST_NAME, EMAIL) and SesSender.applyMergeFields blanks any unresolved tag, so '{{FIRST_NAME}}' becomes an empty string and 'Hi ,' ships to a consultant oncologist. And the brand rule forbids the usual fallback, because 'never use Dear Doctor' is an explicit standing instruction. So this cohort needs a genuinely name-free opening line, written once and reused. Campaign SUBJECT lines are additionally sent raw with no merge pass at all (CampaignService.sendOne:201), so any personalised subject is broken for everyone, not just this cohort.

preSendCohorts.name: P11 Persona Tier Unknown
preSendCohorts.definition: Seniority and specialty: senior consultant, hepatobiliary surgeon, faculty, fellow, resident, medical student, industry. The campaign brief states outright that the list is an unsegmented mix with no clean tagging.
preSendCohorts.sqlOrRule: NEEDS: subscriber.persona VARCHAR(32) and subscriber.persona_confidence. Nothing in the data model carries role, seniority or specialty; the closest existing fields are the free-text source and company columns, neither of which is exposed by SubscriberRepository.search (it filters q, status and listId only). Interim carrier: one static list per persona ('persona-oncologist-senior', 'persona-trainee', 'persona-student'), seeded from the pipeline's category and confidence columns in MASTER_all_emails, and set at import time. Honest caveat: the pipeline's persona buckets exist as 12 June files of 1 to 10 rows each, so this taxonomy was built and never applied at scale.
preSendCohorts.estShare: Effectively 100% unknown today. Even generous extraction from the pipeline exports would cover only the 6,459 confirmed oncologists across the whole 339k universe, of whom an unknown and probably small fraction sit on this 3,363 list.
preSendCohorts.whyDifferent: Because it is unknown, the copy must carry the segmentation instead of the audience data: the layered value stack the brief already prescribes, with the senior hook in the first two lines, the resident hook mid-body and the student hook last. Name this cohort explicitly rather than pretending the list is homogeneous, and use every send as a labelling opportunity: a click on a trial-data link versus a click on a certificate link is the cheapest persona signal available, and it costs nothing but two distinct URLs.

teachingNotes: Cohorts exist before you send anything. Provenance (where the address came from), history (attended, registered, no-showed, never contacted), data quality (verified, risky, catch-all, role account), and record completeness (is there a usable first name) all partition your list on day zero. If your first email treats 3,363 people identically, you have not started segmenting late, you have thrown away segmentation you already owned.

Absence of data is itself a cohort. 'Persona unknown' and 'no platform history' are real, nameable, plannable segments, not gaps to be papered over. Naming them forces the copy to do the work the data cannot, and it stops someone inventing a confident-sounding warm segment out of nothing.

A fresh platform is not a fresh audience. JCF-Mailer's engagement counters are all zero because June went out through Postmark, but the recipients remember being emailed and some of them already opted out. Import the prior suppression history before the first send or you will re-mail people who said no, on a brand new domain with no reputation to absorb it.

Machine opens are not engagement, and this platform already knows it. OpenClassifier splits every open into HUMAN, APPLE_MPP, PROXY or BOT, and only HUMAN counts. MPP fires on delivery whether or not a human ever looked, so it measures iPhone ownership, not interest. Treating it as engagement does three kinds of damage at once: it inflates your open rate (the platform literally publishes inflationFactor so you can see by how much), it corrupts any A/B winner call, and it promotes unread people out of the reminder track, which is the send that actually converts. Branch on clicks, replies and registrations. Report machine opens on their own line.

Zero opens is not zero reads. Images-off clients, corporate gateways and text-only readers never fire the pixel. The largest cohort in most flows is 'delivered and silent', and some of it is reading you. Never suppress on open-silence alone; suppress on the combination of no clicks, no replies and no conversions over several stages.

Negative signals outrank positive ones, without exception and without seniority carve-outs. A complaint, a hard bounce or a reply saying stop ends the relationship no matter how many times that person opened, and no matter how much you want them at the event.

Explicit human intent beats any inferred signal. A reply is better data than a pixel. Yet reply handling is the biggest blind spot in this stack: the inbox is readable but nothing links a reply to a campaign, there is no REPLIED state, and the mailbox credential lives in a browser session so no background job can even look. Until that is fixed, reply triage is a named human duty after every stage, not an automation.

One person, one cohort, per stage. Resolve the precedence chain top to bottom, take the first match, stop, and write the answer down at queue time. Overlapping cohorts produce double sends and unreadable reports, and a cohort recomputed at report time quietly rewrites history so that every stage-over-stage comparison becomes fiction.

Measure the outcome, not the proxy. A click on a registration link is intent; a registration is the result. This platform cannot see registrations at all (the success page records nothing) and it cannot see conversions per variant. Say 'we measured clicks, not registrations' out loud rather than letting a click rate be quoted as a conversion rate. Conversion capture is the smallest of the seven build gaps and the one with the highest return.

Static lists mean every cohort is a job, not a query. There is no saved segment and no re-evaluation, so a cohort is only as current as the last CSV import or SQL materialisation. Date-stamp every list name, rebuild the exclusion lists (registered, suppressed, frequency-capped) immediately before each stage, and assume any list older than one stage is wrong.

Lifetime counters cannot answer per-stage questions. subscriber.total_opened tells you whether someone ever opened; it cannot tell you whether they opened stage 3. Per-stage truth lives in tracking_event joined through recipient_id, filtered to classification='HUMAN'. Never build a branch on the legacy CampaignRecipient.openedAt field, which the codebase itself documents as historically inflated and never retro-corrected.

Deliverability tier controls sequence and volume, not words. Send verified-clean first, in batches, and watch bounce and complaint rates against the 5.0% and 0.5% block thresholds before releasing risky and unverified addresses. One shared sending identity serves every future Horizon edition, so a bad send is not a bad campaign, it is a damaged asset.

Check whether email is actually your growth channel before you optimise it. Of 209 unique attendees on 27 June, 18 were on the 3,363-address emailed list. 191 arrived some other way. That ratio says the forwardable asset, the partner promotion and the peer-to-peer clinician send deserve more attention than a seventh reminder stage, and it is the kind of number a cohort model exists to surface.

Zoom API /meetings/{id}/registrants + the 27 June attendee log (attendeelog_2026_06_27...csv) give C1 and C2; Postmark Activity export (if recoverable) gives C3; horizon-clean.csv minus all three gives C4. POST /api/lists x4 (Horizon-C1-Attendees, C2-NoShow, C3-PriorEngaged, C4-Cold), then POST /api/lists/import per list. Run POST /api/verification/list?listId= on C4 and drop UNDELIVERABLE. Split the 12 blank-first-name rows into a fifth micro-list with no-name copy. Confirm SES identity health via GET /api/overview before anything ships.

stages.flowSummary: Eight stages over 43 days, anchored on a Saturday 19:30 IST Horizon edition (worked example: Sat 26 Sep 2026), replacing a two-blast Postmark send with a cohort-differentiated flow that JCF-Mailer can actually run today. Stage 1 is not one blast: four cohorts cut from real artefacts (Zoom attendee log, Zoom registrant export, prior-engaged, cold remainder of horizon-clean.csv) get four different first emails, sent smallest-and-warmest-first over ten days so the cohort logic doubles as warm-up for the new horizonevent.info sending domain. Stage 2 is a deliberate give with no ask at all (recording plus a one-page clinical takeaway), which is what earns Stage 3's registration ask the right to be direct and gives you a clean intent signal uncontaminated by an offer. Stage 4 is the personal, plain-text, reply-inviting email to the engaged-but-unregistered, with a hard one-business-day human reply SLA because on this list a reply converts at roughly ten times a click. Stage 5 forks on the two different failure modes (opened-but-did-not-click gets agenda depth, never-opened gets exactly one retry at a different hour with a different subject). Stage 6 splits last-chance for non-registrants from join-instructions for registrants, and the Zoom link never touches a non-registrant. Stage 7 forks the post-event mail three ways because attendees, registered-no-shows and engaged-never-registered are three different relationships. Stage 8 sunsets the permanently silent into a dormant list rather than the permanent global_suppression table, which is what protects the domain for the next edition. Because the platform has no journeys, no dynamic segments, no variant column and no conversion tracking, every branch here is a documented human loop: reclassify, pull the HUMAN-classified set out of tracking_event, import it as a new static list, create the stage as its own campaign, schedule it. Each stage is one campaign row, which the UNIQUE(campaignId, subscriberId) constraint forces anyway.

stages.name: Cohort Opener and Domain Warm-Up Wave
stages.purpose: Re-open the relationship at four different temperatures with four different first emails, while using the cohort order as the warm-up ramp for the new horizonevent.info sending domain.
stages.timing: T-26 to T-17, five sends across ten days.
