Two copy constraints that silently void tests if missed. Campaign subjects are passed to SES raw with no merge pass (CampaignService.sendOne:201), so no subject-line personalisation test is possible without a code change. And per-link attribution groups by destination URL string with no link IDs, so any two arms pointing at the same registration URL are literally the same row in GET /api/analytics/links: every arm needs its own UTM-tagged URL or the click data is unreadable.

One last framing point for whoever presents this. The June campaign produced 309 attendees and 163 registrants with no measurement at all. The first honest goal of this programme is not to find a winning subject line, it is to produce the first real open, click, bounce and complaint numbers this organisation has ever had. Treat Horizon IV as calibration, publish the baselines, recompute every n in this document against them, and start making significance claims from Horizon V.

metrics.definition: delivered / sent, where sent = COUNT(campaign_recipient WHERE campaign_id = X AND status = 'SENT') and delivered = sent - bounced. Report separately, never folded in: queue loss = (skipped + failed) / total_recipients. Denominator is SES-accepted sends, NOT queued rows.
metrics.source: GET /api/analytics/summary?campaignId=X -> keys sent, delivered, deliveredRate, failedAllTime, skippedAllTime (analytics/AnalyticsService.java:53-121). Per-recipient truth once SNS is live: message_log.outcome / outcomeAt / serverResponse (MessageLogEntry, 60-day retention), one row per recipient per send.
metrics.realisticTarget: ESTIMATE, no local baseline exists (no bounce or delivery figure for the June Postmark send survives anywhere on this machine). Stage 1 on a 2026-recut scraped list: 94-97%. Stage 3 onward after verification and suppression: 97-99%. Below 94% on stage 1 means the list is older than the 18 Aug 2026 file date suggests.
metrics.trap: 'delivered' here is a subtraction, not a measurement. bounced comes from the email + timestamp heuristic at analytics/AnalyticsAggregateRepository.java:64-83, which the code itself documents as over-counting when two campaigns mailed the same address inside the window. A 7-stage campaign at 3-4 day gaps triggers that condition on every stage after the first, so stages 2-7 will show phantom bounces and artificially depressed delivery. Worse, aws.ses.configurationSet is blank (application.properties:45), so SES publishes no per-message events at all: soft bounces, deferrals and true Delivery events are invisible, and POST /api/sns/ses-events 403s on every payload because jarurat.sns.allowed-topic-arns is unset. Until both are fixed, delivery rate is a lower bound with an unquantified error bar, not a number to report to a funder.

metrics.definition: (skipped + failed) / total_recipients for the stage, split into skipped_suppressed (already on global_suppression at queue or send time), skipped_inflight (suppressed mid-send by skipPendingForEmail) and failed (SES rejected).
metrics.source: GET /api/campaigns/{id}/progress (live: active, total, sent, failed, skipped, lastError) and GET /api/campaigns/{id}/recipients?status=SKIPPED / status=FAILED, paged. campaign_recipient.status + failReason.
metrics.realisticTarget: ESTIMATE: under 1% at stage 1, rising to 3-6% by stage 7 as unsubscribes and bounces accumulate into global_suppression. That rise is healthy, not a fault.
metrics.trap: Rising skipped counts look like a sending failure on the progress endpoint and get reported as one. They are the suppression machinery working correctly at all three enforcement points (queueFromList NOT EXISTS, sendOne re-check, skipPendingForEmail). The real fault signal is FAILED with a repeating failReason, especially MessageRejected or MailFromDomainNotVerified, which SesSender does not retry (SesSender.java:90-107). Watch failReason strings, not the skipped count.

metrics.metric: True open rate (HUMAN-classified, net of Apple MPP and bots)
metrics.definition: reliableOpens / delivered, where reliableOpens = COUNT(DISTINCT recipient_id) in tracking_event WHERE campaign_id = X AND event_type = 'OPEN' AND classification = 'HUMAN'. Use unique openers, never reliableOpenHits.
metrics.source: GET /api/analytics/summary?campaignId=X -> reliableOpens, reliableOpenHits, openRate. Bucket composition at GET /api/analytics/classifier?campaignId=X. Backing table tracking_event (analytics/TrackingEvent.java), classifier at analytics/OpenClassifier.java:115-165.
metrics.realisticTarget: ESTIMATE for an unsegmented Indian clinician list, 88% free-mail, first contact in ~2 months: stage 1 HUMAN open rate 20-30%; stages 2-5 decaying to 14-22%; day-of reminder spikes back to 25-35% on a much smaller audience. Treat anything above 40% as a classifier problem, not a copy win.
metrics.trap: Three separate lies. (1) The legacy number is inflated: GET /api/campaigns and GET /api/overview still serve CampaignService.stats, computed from CampaignRecipient.openedAt with no classification (services/CampaignService.java:353-387). The platform publishes the gap itself as unfilteredOpenRate and inflationFactor. Ban the legacy endpoints from every report; quote inflationFactor once per stage as the reason. (2) The HUMAN number under-counts and is a FLOOR, not a truth: Apple MPP opens include real readers, and any recipient with images off never fires the pixel at all. Never say 'only 22% read it'; say 'at least 22% opened with images loaded'. (3) On this list the dominant client is Gmail, whose image proxy fetches on render and is counted HUMAN unless the fetch lands inside analytics.prefetchWindowSeconds (default 3, OpenClassifier.java:140-151). Gmail proxy caching also suppresses repeat fetches, so open HITS undercount badly while unique openers hold up. Sensitivity test before you trust the number: raise prefetchWindowSeconds to 10, POST /api/analytics/reclassify, re-read. If the open rate moves more than 2 points, the number is fragile and must be reported as a range. Reset the property afterwards and record which setting produced each published figure, because reclassify rewrites history and does NOT retro-correct the legacy openedAt column (OpenTrackingService.java:118-122).

metrics.metric: Classifier composition (MPP / PROXY / BOT share) as the open-rate health check
metrics.definition: mppOpens / (reliableOpens + mppOpens + proxyOpens + botOpens), and the same for proxy and bot, per stage. Track stage over stage as a trend, not as a level.
metrics.source: GET /api/analytics/classifier?campaignId=X (bucket counts plus the live classifier config) and the mppOpens / botOpens / proxyOpens keys of GET /api/analytics/summary.
metrics.realisticTarget: ESTIMATE: APPLE_MPP 8-18% of opens on this list (low versus a Western list because free-mail here is gmail and rediff heavy, not iCloud). BOT 5-15%, concentrated in the first 3 seconds after send from institutional security scanners. A BOT share above 25% means a corporate scanner is chewing the list, or a link checker is walking your tracked URLs.
metrics.trap: This composition is stable per audience but NOT per stage. A jump in BOT share between stages usually means a mailbox provider started pre-scanning you, which is a deliverability signal disguised as an analytics artefact. A jump in PROXY share usually means a forwarding chain. Read this table before you read the open rate, every single stage, or you will attribute a filtering change to your subject line.

metrics.definition: reliableClicks / delivered, where reliableClicks = COUNT(DISTINCT recipient_id) in tracking_event WHERE event_type = 'CLICK' AND classification = 'HUMAN'.
metrics.source: GET /api/analytics/summary?campaignId=X -> reliableClicks, reliableClickHits, botClicks, clickRate. Per-destination breakdown at GET /api/analytics/links?campaignId=X (url, clicks, unique, share) and the 'links' key of GET /api/campaigns/{id}.
metrics.realisticTarget: ESTIMATE: 2.5-5.0% on the registration CTA for stages 1-3; 4-8% on the final reminder and day-of stages, computed on the shrunken audience they are sent to.
metrics.trap: Attribution is by destination URL STRING only. There are no link ids and no labels (models/ClickEvent.java, TrackingEventRepository.java:70-91), so a header button and a footer link pointing at the same registration URL are one row in topLinks and cannot be separated. If you want to know which CTA position worked, the URLs must differ, which means the UTM convention below is not optional polish, it is the entire click-attribution scheme. Second trap: clicks inside the prefetch window or from a scanner UA are logged as BOT and excluded from every rate (OpenClassifier.java:171-198), which is correct but means botClicks is a real deliverability signal you should read, not a zero to ignore.

metrics.definition: unique HUMAN clickers / unique HUMAN openers, same campaign.
metrics.realisticTarget: ESTIMATE: 12-20% for a specialist webinar invitation to a matched clinical audience. Below 8% means the subject earned the open and the body did not earn the click, which on this list usually means the value stack was buried below the first screen.
metrics.trap: Biased HIGH by construction. The denominator is the filtered HUMAN open floor, while the numerator can contain clickers whose open was never recorded (images off, or the pixel classified MPP while the click classified HUMAN). CTOR above roughly 35% on this list is almost always denominator collapse, not persuasion. Always publish clickRate alongside it; if CTOR rises while clickRate falls, the copy did not improve, the open measurement decayed.

metrics.definition: registrants_matched / unique HUMAN clickers on the registration URL for that stage, where registrants_matched = COUNT(DISTINCT email) present in the Zoom registrant export AND present in that stage's clicker set AND whose Zoom Registration Time is after the click timestamp.
metrics.source: NO platform source. Conversion tracking does not exist: GET /api/mailer/success (controllers/TrackingController.java:84-87) renders a static thank-you page and records nothing, and there is no inbound conversion API on PublicApiV1. Build it: the audit's small-effort sketch (conversion_event table plus ?token= on /api/mailer/success plus POST /api/v1/conversions). Until then, join the Zoom registrant CSV against GET /api/campaigns/{id}/export?status=SENT and GET /api/analytics/links on the email column.
metrics.realisticTarget: ESTIMATE anchored on the one real local datum: at June send time 163 Zoom registrants existed and 128 of them were on the 3,367-address emailed list. Expect 30-45% of unique registration-link clickers to complete Zoom registration; the Zoom form is a second funnel with its own 55-70% completion. Whole-list registration rate 4-8% cumulative across all 7 stages.
metrics.trap: Four ways this lies. (1) Multi-touch collapse: at 3-4 day gaps a doctor clicks stage 3 and registers after stage 5. Fix the rule in advance and write it down: attribute to the LATEST stage whose HUMAN click precedes the Zoom registration timestamp, and publish the rule with the number. (2) Off-channel registrants: in June, 35 of 163 registrants (21%) were not on the emailed list at all. Report 'unattributed registrants' as its own line every stage, never silently allocate them to email. (3) Email-join failure: a doctor emailed at a hospital address who registers with a personal gmail is invisible to the join and shows up as unattributed. Estimate the size of this by checking how many unattributed registrants share a surname with an emailed contact. (4) Clicking is intent, not completion. Never report link clicks as conversions, which is exactly the substitution the platform's own static success page invites.

metrics.definition: new unique registrants first attributable to stage N / delivered at stage N. 'New' means the email does not appear in the registrant export snapshot taken immediately before stage N sent.
metrics.source: Requires a pre-stage Zoom registrant snapshot (export at T minus 1 hour for every stage) joined to the post-stage export. Nothing in JCF-Mailer stores this; it is a manual artefact you must create, and it cannot be reconstructed after the fact.
metrics.realisticTarget: ESTIMATE: stage 1 (save the date) 0.8-1.5%; stages 2-3 0.5-1.0% each; stage 5 final reminder 1.0-2.0%; day-of stage 0.3-0.8%. Declining incremental value across the middle stages is normal and expected.
metrics.trap: Late stages inherit demand manufactured by early stages, so last-touch attribution systematically over-credits reminders and under-credits the save-the-date. Do not use this metric to delete stage 1. Use it only with a kill rule fixed in advance: drop a stage from the next cycle only if it adds under 0.5% new registrants AND its unsubscribe rate exceeds the campaign mean AND its complaint count is non-zero.

metrics.definition: distinct human replies / delivered, split into three buckets fixed in advance: interested/question, decline or opt-out-by-reply, and automated (out of office, delivery notification, mailbox-full).
metrics.source: NO platform source. Reply detection does not exist (no In-Reply-To capture, no REPLIED status, no campaign_reply table; mail/MessageSummary.java carries no threading field, and MailboxAccess holds the mailbox secret in a browser HttpSession so no background job can read the inbox). Config-only workaround that needs zero code: Campaign.replyTo is per-campaign overridable (models/Campaign.java:20-21), so give each of the 7 stages its own plus-addressed reply alias, for example horizon+s3@jarurat.care, and count via GET /api/mail/search. Verify the alias actually lands in the Stalwart mailbox with a live test before stage 1; do not assume plus addressing is enabled.
metrics.realisticTarget: ESTIMATE: 0.3-1.5% on stages 1-3 for a professional list where the sender is a named human, dropping under 0.3% on reminder stages. The earlier Zoho drip bot treated a reply as the stop condition, so replies are operationally load-bearing here, not just a vanity number.
metrics.trap: Manual counting rots fast. Recipients who hit Reply All or whose client ignores Reply-To will land on admin@jarurat.care or partnership@jarurat.care instead, so the per-stage alias undercounts; sample the main inbox weekly and apply a correction factor. Auto-responders inflate the raw count by 2-5x on a hospital-heavy list. And critically: a reply saying 'remove me' is a legal opt-out under DPDP framing and must be pushed manually to POST /api/suppressions/add?email= the same day, because nothing automates that path.

metrics.definition: unsubscribed / delivered for the stage. Cumulative campaign churn from unsubscribes = distinct global_suppression rows with reason = 'UNSUBSCRIBED' created between stage 1 send start and stage 7 completion, divided by mailable list size at stage 1.
metrics.source: GET /api/analytics/summary?campaignId=X -> unsubscribed, unsubscribeRate. Underlying table global_suppression (models/GlobalSuppression.java, email as PK, reason enum). Listing at GET /api/suppressions?q=.
metrics.realisticTarget: ESTIMATE: 0.2-0.5% per stage on stages 1-3, under 0.3% on later stages. Cumulative 1.5-3.0% across all 7 stages is a healthy outcome for a list this cold. Any single stage above 0.8% is a frequency or relevance failure and should stop the next stage until the copy is re-read.
metrics.trap: global_suppression is keyed on email with a single timestamp and no campaign id, so per-stage attribution is the same timestamp heuristic that distorts bounce attribution, and it breaks when two stages run inside the same window. Second trap: Gmail and Yahoo one-click List-Unsubscribe-Post (SesSender.java:117-127, TrackingController.java:78) fires with NO open and NO click event, so a recipient can unsubscribe while appearing totally unengaged. Expect unsubscribe rate to look high relative to measured engagement; that is the measurement, not the audience. Third: unsubscribes are a lagging quality signal that is far cheaper than complaints. A rising unsubscribe rate with a flat complaint rate is the system working.

metrics.definition: complained / delivered, per stage and cumulative across the campaign. Cumulative is the number SES actually enforces on.
metrics.source: GET /api/analytics/summary?campaignId=X -> complained, complaintRate, complaintDangerLine (0.1). Underlying: Subscriber.status = 'COMPLAINED' and global_suppression reason = 'COMPLAINT', written by SuppressionService. Real source of truth for a gmail-heavy list: Google Postmaster Tools spam rate for horizonevent.info, which is external to the platform.
metrics.realisticTarget: Hard ceilings, not estimates: SES issues a warning at 0.1% and places the account under review at 0.5%. Gmail's bulk sender rules target 0.10% and treat 0.30% as never-exceed. Target under 0.05% per stage. The platform's own SafetyCheckService blocks at complaintBlockPct 0.5, which is far too late; tighten it to 0.1 before stage 1.
metrics.trap: Systematically UNDER-reported on this specific list. Gmail does not operate a per-message complaint feedback loop back to SES for individual users, and roughly 88% of this list is free-mail with gmail dominant, so a large share of 'this is spam' clicks will never appear in your complaint count at all. Your measured complaint rate can read 0.02% while Google Postmaster Tools shows 0.4% and your gmail delivery quietly collapses into the Promotions tab and then the spam folder. Treat the in-platform complaint rate as a floor and Postmaster Tools as the operative number. Additionally, the SNS complaint path is inert today (SnsMessageVerifier throws when allowed-topic-arns is empty), so the only live complaint feed is the 15-minute account-level SES suppression poll, which is delayed and cannot be attributed to a stage except by timestamp.

metrics.metric: Bounce rate, split by recipient domain family
metrics.definition: bounced / sent overall, and separately for each domain family: gmail.com, yahoo/ymail, hotmail/outlook/live, rediffmail, other free-mail, institutional (.edu, .edu.in, .ac.in, hospital domains), everything else. Hard versus soft split once SES events are wired.
metrics.source: Overall: GET /api/analytics/summary -> bounced, bounceRate, bounceDangerLine (2.0). By domain: no endpoint exists. Export GET /api/campaigns/{id}/export?status=SENT, join to global_suppression reason='BOUNCE' and to verification_result, and group on the domain substring locally. Once configurationSet is set, message_log.outcome gives per-recipient bounce type.
metrics.realisticTarget: Hard ceiling: SES places an account at risk at 5% and may pause sending near 10%; the platform's SafetyCheckService blocks at 5.0, and AnalyticsService already publishes a bounceDangerLine of 2.0. Stop-and-think line is 2%, not 5%. ESTIMATE for the horizon-clean.csv recut (3,363 rows, verified locally in Aug 2026 but never mailed from this domain): 1-3% overall on stage 1, under 0.5% by stage 3. Free-mail domains should bounce well under 1%; the institutional tail (47 academic addresses) and the 167-domain long tail is where the bounces will be.
metrics.trap: The aggregate hides the failure. A 2.5% overall bounce rate made of 0.4% gmail plus 40% on one hospital domain is a completely different problem from 2.5% spread evenly, and only the domain split tells you which. There is no domain-level suppression in the platform, so acting on this means manually adding addresses via POST /api/suppressions/add?email= per address. Second trap: without configurationSet, soft bounces and deferrals never surface at all, so a domain that is deferring you into oblivion looks like clean delivery.

metrics.definition: stage churn = (unsubscribes + hard bounces + complaints attributed to the stage) / mailable list size measured immediately BEFORE that stage sent. Campaign churn = the same numerator summed over all 7 stages, over the stage 1 mailable size.
metrics.source: Mailable size from ListMemberRepository.countMailable (surfaced on GET /api/lists and in GET /api/campaigns/{id}). Numerator from GET /api/suppressions?q= plus Subscriber.status counts via GET /api/subscribers?status=BOUNCED / UNSUBSCRIBED / COMPLAINED.
metrics.realisticTarget: ESTIMATE: under 6% cumulative across 7 stages for a list of this provenance. Above 10% means the list was staler than the 18 Aug 2026 file date implies, and the next cycle must start from re-verification rather than re-sending.
metrics.trap: Nothing in the platform stores history. countMailable is a live count, subscriber status counts are live, and suppression rows have only a creation timestamp. If you do not snapshot mailable size and status counts to a dated CSV immediately before every one of the 7 stages, per-stage churn becomes permanently uncomputable the moment stage N+1 sends. This is the single most commonly lost measurement in this platform, and it costs nothing to prevent.

metrics.definition: lift = registration_rate(treatment) - registration_rate(holdout), where registration_rate = distinct emails in the Zoom registrant export that appear in that group / group size. Report with a two-proportion z test and the absolute counts, never the percentage alone.
metrics.source: No platform source. Holdout is a static mailing list built once, excluded from all 7 stage lists, and never sent to. Compute from the holdout list export against the final Zoom registrant CSV.
metrics.realisticTarget: Power math, defensible: with 3,363 mailable, a 10% holdout is 336 held out and 3,027 treated. If treatment registers at 6% and the holdout baseline is 1% (holdouts can still find the event through LinkedIn, WhatsApp and forwards, which is exactly the point), the standard error is about 1.38 points and z is about 3.6, comfortably significant. At a 5% holdout (168 people) the same effect gives z of about 2.7, still significant but with no margin. Recommend 10%. The cost of a 10% holdout at a 6% treatment rate is roughly 17 forgone registrations across the campaign; that is the price of ever knowing whether the email programme works.
metrics.trap: Contamination is guaranteed and one-directional. A treated doctor forwards the invite to a held-out colleague, and a held-out registrant is counted as organic when email actually caused it. This biases measured lift DOWNWARD, so treat your lift number as a conservative floor and say so. Second trap: the holdout must be drawn at random from the whole mailable list before any stage sends and frozen; drawing it after stage 1, or drawing it from the tail of the CSV, converts the measurement into noise. Third: only run the holdout once per campaign, not per stage; a per-stage holdout of 336 has nowhere near enough registrations to resolve.

metrics.metric: A/B arm delta (subject line) with an honest power floor
metrics.definition: metric(arm A) - metric(arm B) on identical audiences, where arms are two static lists split by a deterministic local hash of the email address, frozen once and reused for all 7 stages, and each stage is sent as two separate campaigns (HZN-S3-A, HZN-S3-B) because the platform has no variant dimension at all.
metrics.source: GET /api/analytics/campaigns?days= (AnalyticsService.byCampaign) gives per-campaign rows, which under this scheme are per-arm rows. Everything already works; no build needed, at the cost of 14 campaign objects.
metrics.realisticTarget: Power math on n = 1,500 per arm (10% holdout removed, split in two): at a 25% baseline open rate the minimum detectable difference at 80% power and 95% confidence is about 3.1 percentage points. At a 5% baseline registration rate the minimum detectable difference is about 1.6 points, which is a 32% relative change. Conclusion to state up front: this list size can settle subject-line and open-rate questions, and cannot settle conversion questions. Do not run a body-copy test expecting a registration verdict.
metrics.trap: Two failure modes. (1) Peeking: reading the delta four hours in and declaring a winner, when opens on an Indian clinician list keep arriving for 48-72 hours. Fix the read time in advance at T plus 48 hours per stage. (2) Re-randomising: if the arms are re-split each stage, cumulative fatigue effects mix across arms and every stage-over-stage comparison becomes meaningless. Freeze the split, keep the seed and the assignment CSV, and check arm balance on the pre-campaign covariates you have (domain family, verification verdict, prior attendee status) before stage 1 rather than explaining an imbalance afterwards.

deliverability: AUTHENTICATION, all three, on the actual sending domain horizonevent.info before any stage 1 send. SPF: TXT at the root, v=spf1 include:amazonses.com -all. DKIM: SES Easy DKIM at 2048-bit, three CNAME records, verified. Custom MAIL FROM subdomain bounce.horizonevent.info with MX 10 feedback-smtp.ap-south-1.amazonses.com priority 10 and its own SPF TXT, which is what buys you SPF alignment rather than just an SPF pass. Verify all of it through the platform rather than by eye: SesSender.identityHealth (SesSender.java:277-311) already reports DKIM and MAIL FROM status and it surfaces on GET /api/overview. A blank or FAILED MAIL FROM status is a stop-the-campaign condition.

DMARC posture, staged. Publish _dmarc.horizonevent.info as v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@jarurat.care; fo=1; adkim=r; aspf=r at least 7 days before stage 1 and actually read the aggregate reports. Move to p=quarantine; pct=25 only after two stages have sent with zero alignment failures in the rua data, then pct=100. Do NOT go to p=reject during a live 7-stage campaign; a reject policy plus an unnoticed alignment break equals total delivery loss with no warning. jarurat.care itself should already be at p=quarantine or better since it is the reply and brand domain.

SES CONFIGURATION SET is the precondition for every deliverability number in this plan. aws.ses.configurationSet is blank today (application.properties:45) and SesSender.java:139-147 notes this means SES publishes no per-message events at all. Create a configuration set, attach an event destination for Send, Delivery, Bounce, Complaint, Reject and DeliveryDelay to an SNS topic, set aws.ses.configurationSet, and set jarurat.sns.allowed-topic-arns to that topic ARN so SnsMessageVerifier stops throwing and POST /api/sns/ses-events stops returning 403 on every payload. Confirm with a real signed test event, not a curl of unsigned JSON. Without this the only bounce feed is the 15-minute account-level SES suppression poll (SuppressionService.java:89-114), which is delayed, account-wide, and attributable to a stage only by a timestamp heuristic the code itself flags as over-counting.

WARM-UP RAMP on a domain with no meaningful send history. Concrete daily volumes, spread over the six days before stage 1 goes wide, sending the real stage 1 copy in ascending slices ordered by list quality (past attendees from the 309-row 27 June log first, then the 163 prior registrants, then verified DELIVERABLE institutional, then verified free-mail, then the rest): Day 1 = 250, Day 2 = 500, Day 3 = 1,000, Day 4 = 0 (hold and read bounce, complaint and Google Postmaster Tools), Day 5 = 2,000, Day 6 = 3,027 (full list minus the 336-address holdout). Cumulative six-day volume about 6,777. Check GetSendQuota first: if the account is still in the SES sandbox or on a low daily quota, none of this runs. From stage 2 onward, full volume per stage with a minimum 3-day gap and a hard cap of 3 emails per contact per rolling 7 days, which is the cap the existing campaign brief already specifies.

PER-HOUR THROTTLE. aws.ses.maxSendRate is 12/s and process-wide, shared with transactional mail (application.properties:46); at that rate the whole 3,363 list lands in 4.7 minutes, which is the single most aggressive thing a cold domain can do. Set maxSendRate to 2/s for the warm-up and stages 1-2, then 5/s. Per-campaign pacing does not exist (audit gap 7), so implement pacing by construction: split each stage into chunk sub-lists of 500 and schedule one chunk per hour inside a fixed send window of 10:00-13:00 and 18:30-21:00 IST. That is 5-6 chunks per day, a natural ceiling of 2,500-3,000 sends/day, and it matches the batch-of-500 stagger the existing campaign brief already recommends. Scheduling granularity is about 60 seconds (runDueCampaigns polls at fixedDelay 60000), which is fine at hourly spacing.

RUN EXACTLY ONE APPLICATION INSTANCE for the duration of the campaign. CampaignService.runDueCampaigns has no scheduler lock and no cross-instance guard, so two instances both fire the same scheduled campaign, and the (campaignId, subscriberId) unique constraint prevents duplicate ROWS but not duplicate SENDS from a race. Verify the instance count before every scheduled stage. A duplicate blast to 3,000 clinicians is a complaint-rate event you cannot undo.

COMPLAINT CEILINGS, enforced by SES and by Gmail, both. SES: 0.1% is a warning, 0.5% puts the account under review. Gmail bulk sender rules: 0.10% target, 0.30% never-exceed. The platform's SafetyCheckService currently blocks at complaintBlockPct 0.5 and bounceBlockPct 5.0 (campaignsplus/SafetyCheckService.java:132-134), which are the point-of-no-return values, not operating limits. Tighten them before stage 1 to complaintBlockPct 0.1 and bounceBlockPct 2.0, matching the complaintDangerLine 0.1 and bounceDangerLine 2.0 that AnalyticsService already publishes. The gate runs on the caller's thread at CampaignService.java:112, so scheduled stages are gated too.

BOUNCE CEILING AND OPERATING LINES. SES at-risk at 5%, possible pause approaching 10%. Operating rules for this campaign: under 1% cumulative is green, continue; 1-2% is amber, finish the current chunk and re-verify the unsent remainder before the next chunk; over 2% is red, cancel the remaining scheduled chunks; over 5% is stop the campaign and do not send again until the list has been rebuilt. Compute these on cumulative campaign bounce, not per stage, because that is what SES enforces on.

LIST HYGIENE using the platform's own verifier, before stage 1 and again before any stage that adds addresses. Run POST /api/verification/list?listId= over the full list, watch GET /api/verification/progress?key=, export via GET /api/verification/export?listId=. Drop UNDELIVERABLE outright (queueFromList already excludes them at CampaignRecipientRepository.java:53-72, but removing them keeps the denominators honest). Hold RISKY and catch-all addresses out of the warm-up and stages 1-2 entirely and add them at stage 3 only if cumulative bounce is under 1%. Re-verify anything not mailed in 90 days. Note the composition you are working with: 3,363 rows, 167 domains, about 88% free-mail, only 47 academic, so the bounce risk is concentrated in the institutional long tail, not in the gmail bulk.

GOOGLE POSTMASTER TOOLS is not optional on a list that is roughly 88% free-mail with gmail dominant. Verify horizonevent.info in Postmaster Tools at the same time you publish DMARC, because it needs the DNS proof and it needs volume history before it renders anything useful (roughly 200+ messages/day to a domain before the reputation and spam-rate panels populate, which the ramp above satisfies from day 3). Postmaster spam rate is the operative complaint number for this campaign; the in-platform complaint rate is a floor because Gmail does not run a per-user feedback loop back to SES. Amber at 0.10%, red at 0.30%.

SEED AND PLACEMENT LIST, about 15 addresses, in its own mailing list, never counted in any denominator: 5 gmail, 2 yahoo, 2 outlook/hotmail, 2 rediffmail, 1 icloud, 3 institutional or hospital-hosted. Send every stage's copy to the seeds with POST /api/campaigns/test-send before the first real chunk (tracking is forced off for test sends, which is exactly what you want) and record inbox versus Promotions versus Spam per provider in a dated sheet. Placement is the metric that open rate cannot see, and it is the earliest warning you get.

MID-SEND BOUNCE SPIKE PROCEDURE, ordered, because there is no pause: Campaign.status documents PAUSED but nothing in the codebase ever sets it. (1) The real stop control is the chunk boundary, which is why hourly 500-address chunks exist. On a spike, POST /api/campaigns/cancel-schedule?id= on every remaining scheduled chunk campaign; that halts the stage cleanly. (2) For a spike inside a running chunk, the only true kill switches are blunt: disable account sending in the SES console, or stop the application process. Losing at most 500 in-flight sends is the designed worst case. (3) Read GET /api/campaigns/{id}/progress for the lastError string and GET /api/campaigns/{id}/recipients?status=FAILED for repeating failReason values; MessageRejected, MailFromDomainNotVerified and AccountSuspended are never retried by SesSender and mean stop immediately. (4) Split the bounces by domain before drawing any conclusion; a single hospital domain rejecting everything is a whitelisting problem, an even spread is a list-age or reputation problem. (5) Re-verify the entire unsent remainder before resuming, and resume at half the previous chunk rate. (6) Trigger thresholds inside a single 500-chunk: more than 10 bounces (2%) halts the next chunk; more than 25 (5%) halts the stage. Honest caveat: until the configuration set and SNS are live, none of this is observable in real time, because permanent bounces only surface after the 15-minute suppression poll and soft bounces never surface at all. Wiring SNS is what converts this procedure from theatre into an actual control.

SENDING IDENTITY DISCIPLINE. There is one envelope From for the whole platform; only fromName and replyTo are per-campaign (models/Campaign.java:20-21). Pick one From and do not change it mid-campaign, because reputation accrues to the address. Keep the marketing domain (horizonevent.info) separate from transactional and staff mail on jarurat.care so a campaign complaint spike cannot poison operational email. Do not send campaign mail and transactional mail through the same rate limiter during warm-up windows, since maxSendRate is shared process-wide.

COMPLIANCE FOOTER, non-negotiable and already partly enforced. The platform force-appends an unsubscribe footer whenever {{UNSUBSCRIBE_LINK}} is absent and sets List-Unsubscribe plus List-Unsubscribe-Post one-click headers (SesSender.java:117-127, 181-193), so one-click unsubscribe is satisfied. Add explicitly in the visible footer: the registered NGO name Jarurat Care Foundation, registration number U87200UT2023NPL016406, a postal address, and a one-line DPDP-Act consent statement saying why this address is being contacted. This is the cheapest complaint-rate reduction available and it costs one paragraph.
instrumentation: 1. Freeze the platform. Confirm exactly one application instance is running and will stay that way for the campaign (runDueCampaigns has no cross-instance lock). Record the deployed commit, and change no analytics configuration after stage 1 without recording the change alongside the numbers it affects.

2. Publish and verify DNS for horizonevent.info: DKIM (3 CNAMEs, 2048-bit), SPF with -all, custom MAIL FROM subdomain with its MX and SPF, DMARC p=none with a real rua mailbox. Confirm through GET /api/overview / SesSender.identityHealth, not by eye. Blocking: nothing else matters if this is wrong.

3. Wire SES events end to end: create the configuration set, attach the SNS event destination (Send, Delivery, Bounce, Complaint, Reject, DeliveryDelay), set aws.ses.configurationSet, set jarurat.sns.allowed-topic-arns, and prove POST /api/sns/ses-events returns 200 on a genuinely signed test event instead of the 403 it returns today. This is the single highest-value item on the list: without it, delivery, bounce and complaint are all inferred from a timestamp heuristic the code itself documents as over-counting.

4. Tighten the safety gate and the throttle: SafetyCheckService bounceBlockPct 5.0 -> 2.0, complaintBlockPct 0.5 -> 0.1, aws.ses.maxSendRate 12 -> 2 for warm-up. Record the old values so they can be restored.

5. Verify the list: POST /api/verification/list?listId= over all 3,363 addresses, export the results, delete UNDELIVERABLE, and park RISKY plus catch-all into a separate wave-2 list that does not send until stage 3.

6. Build the HOLDOUT first, before any other split. Draw 10% (336 addresses) uniformly at random from the verified mailable list using a recorded random seed, materialise as a static list named horizon-holdout-2026, and exclude it from every stage list for the whole campaign. Save the seed and the assignment CSV. A holdout drawn later, or drawn from the end of a file, is not a holdout.

7. Build the A/B arms from the remaining 3,027 by a deterministic local hash of the lowercased email (for example first 4 bytes of SHA-256, even/odd), materialise as horizon-armA and horizon-armB, and FREEZE them. The same person must stay in the same arm across all 7 stages, because the platform has no variant column and arm identity exists only in these two static lists. Check arm balance on domain family, verification verdict and prior-attendee flag before stage 1.

8. Cut the chunk lists: split each arm into 500-address chunk lists, named HZN-S{n}-{arm}-C{k}, so pacing, send windows and the mid-send stop control all exist as list structure rather than as features the platform lacks.

9. Snapshot the baseline to dated CSVs: countMailable per list, subscriber counts by status, full global_suppression export, and the pre-campaign Zoom registrant export. Nothing in JCF-Mailer keeps history, so churn, incremental registrations and holdout lift all become permanently uncomputable if this snapshot is skipped. Repeat this snapshot immediately before every stage.

10. Fix the UTM and link conventions, then apply them mechanically. Every destination URL must be unique per (stage, arm, CTA position) because per-link attribution groups on the URL string with no link ids or labels. Convention: ?utm_source=jcfmailer&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=horizon_{event}_{yyyymm}&utm_content=s{stage}_{arm}_{cta}. Keep utm_content the only varying part so the local grouping script is trivial. Do NOT attempt to embed a per-recipient token in a link today: campaign merge resolves only NAME, FIRST_NAME and EMAIL, and click rewriting URL-encodes the href before the merge pass runs, so a token inside a URL will not resolve. Verify whatever you choose against GET /api/campaigns/{id}/rendered before trusting it.

11. Stand up the conversion path. Preferred: build the small-effort conversion capture (conversion_event table, ?token= on GET /api/mailer/success, POST /api/v1/conversions on the API-key-authed PublicApiV1) so the platform learns who actually registered. Fallback if it is not built in time: lock the Zoom registrant export cadence in writing (T minus 1 hour before every stage, T plus 24 hours after every stage, plus daily), and fix the attribution rule in advance (latest HUMAN click preceding the Zoom registration timestamp, unattributed reported separately). The fallback only works if the pre-stage snapshots actually get taken, which is why item 9 precedes it.

12. Stand up reply capture. Config-only version: assign each of the 7 stages its own Campaign.replyTo plus-addressed alias (horizon+s1@ .. horizon+s7@jarurat.care) and prove with a live test that the alias reaches the Stalwart mailbox and that the tag survives in the delivered headers. Confirm someone can and will read GET /api/mail/search per stage, since MailboxAccess requires a human-unlocked session and no background job can do it. Define the three reply buckets and the same-day rule for pushing opt-out-by-reply into POST /api/suppressions/add.

13. Validate the creative mechanically for every stage: POST /api/campaignsplus/templates/validate (merge tags, Gmail 102KB clip, unsubscribe presence) and then GET /api/campaigns/{id}/rendered to read the exact HTML SES will receive. Two known traps to check by eye in the rendered output: unresolved merge tags render as empty string, and campaign SUBJECT lines get no merge pass at all (CampaignService.sendOne passes the raw subject to SES), so a {{FIRST_NAME}} in a subject ships literally.

14. Seed send: POST /api/campaigns/test-send to all 15 seed addresses, record inbox/Promotions/Spam per provider, and only then release warm-up day 1. Repeat the seed send for every stage whose copy or link set changed.

15. Write and dry-run the analytics pull script BEFORE stage 1, against a throwaway test campaign: GET /api/analytics/summary, /series, /links, /clients, /campaigns and /classifier, saved to dated JSON. Include GET /api/analytics/classifier output every time, because the classifier config is part of the result. Explicitly exclude GET /api/campaigns and GET /api/overview from the reporting pipeline; they serve the legacy unclassified open rate and quoting them once will contaminate every comparison afterwards.

16. Establish the reclassify ritual: POST /api/analytics/reclassify after each stage's 72-hour read, and run the prefetchWindowSeconds 3 versus 10 sensitivity check once on stage 1 so you know how fragile the open rate is on this audience before you start drawing conclusions from it.
postMortem: 1. Did the measurement survive? For each of the 7 stages, do we have a pre-stage mailable snapshot, a pre-stage and post-stage Zoom registrant export, and a saved analytics JSON with the classifier config attached? Any stage missing one of these cannot be included in the comparisons below, and we should say which and why before we say anything else.

2. What did SES and Gmail actually think of us? Final cumulative bounce rate, complaint rate, and the Google Postmaster Tools domain reputation and spam-rate curve across the whole campaign. Did we ever cross 2% bounce or 0.1% complaint, and if so what did we do inside the next hour?

3. Where did the bounces concentrate by domain family, and how many of those addresses had been marked DELIVERABLE by our own verifier? That ratio is the honest accuracy score for the verification step and it decides whether next cycle starts from verification or from a rebuild.

4. What was the true HUMAN open rate per stage, and what did the legacy unclassified number claim? Report the inflationFactor per stage. If anyone quoted a number from GET /api/campaigns or the dashboard during the campaign, identify where that number ended up.

5. Did the classifier composition shift stage over stage? A rising BOT or PROXY share is a filtering event, not a copy event. Correlate any composition shift against the seed-placement sheet for the same date.

6. Which stage produced the most NEW registrants per delivered message, and which stage produced the fewest? Apply the kill rule as written (under 0.5% new registrants AND above-mean unsubscribe AND non-zero complaints) rather than re-deciding it now that the numbers are in.

7. What is the click-to-registration conversion, and what fraction of registrants were unattributed to any email? Compare the unattributed share against the June figure of 35 of 163 (21%). If it moved a lot in either direction, what changed off-channel?

8. What is the holdout lift, with absolute counts, the z statistic, and an explicit statement of the contamination direction? State plainly whether the campaign beat doing nothing, and by how many registrations in whole numbers.

9. Did the A/B arms separate on open rate, and was the gap larger than the 3.1-point minimum detectable difference? For any metric where the gap is below the detectable floor, record 'not enough data' rather than a winner. Did anyone read the delta before T plus 48 hours?

10. What did unsubscribes and replies actually say? Read every reply and every unsubscribe reason by hand. On a list this size that is a few dozen items and it is the highest-signal qualitative data the campaign produced. Categorise into wrong-audience, too-frequent, not-relevant-this-topic, and consent-objection.
11. What was total list churn, and what is the mailable list size we are left with for the next cycle? Compare to the 3,363 we started with and to the 3,367 the June send used.

12. Which of the seven build gaps actually bit us, ranked by how much measurement they cost? Concretely: what would per-recipient conversion capture, reply detection and a variant column have told us that we now cannot recover?

13. Where did the send-time operating discipline break: any duplicate sends, any chunk that ran outside the send window, any stage sent from a second app instance, any stage where the safety gate blocked or should have blocked?

14. What did we promise recipients and what did they get? Did every registrant receive the certificate, the recording and the follow-up, and is that promise reflected anywhere in the metrics we optimised? A campaign that hits its registration target and misses its delivery promise has not worked.

15. What are the three changes for the next cycle, in build order, with the measurement each one unlocks named explicitly? Nothing goes on the list unless it changes a number we could not compute this time.
teachingNotes: Raw open rate is a broken metric and this platform is unusual in admitting it. Apple Mail Privacy Protection fetches the tracking pixel for the recipient whether or not anyone reads the mail, and corporate security scanners fetch every link and image before the human sees it. JCF-Mailer's OpenClassifier sorts every hit into HUMAN, APPLE_MPP, PROXY or BOT and only HUMAN counts as engagement, which is the right call. But the platform still runs two reporting stacks side by side: the classified one at /api/analytics/*, and a legacy unclassified one that powers GET /api/campaigns and GET /api/overview and reports the inflated rate straight off CampaignRecipient.openedAt. Both are on screen. Pick the classified stack, say so in writing, and never mix the two in one document.

Understand the direction of each error before you argue with a number. The HUMAN open rate is a FLOOR: it excludes real people reading through MPP and everyone with images off. Click-to-open rate is biased HIGH because its denominator is that floor. Complaint rate is a floor because Gmail does not feed individual complaints back to SES. Delivery rate is currently an over-subtraction because bounces are attributed by a timestamp heuristic that double-counts in multi-stage campaigns. Knowing the sign of the bias is more useful than knowing the number.

Denominators decide arguments. Open rate over delivered and open rate over sent differ by the whole bounce rate; on a stage 1 send with a 3% bounce that is a full percentage point of apparent open rate. Write the denominator into the metric name in every report (openRate_of_delivered, clickRate_of_delivered, CTOR_of_reliableOpens) so nobody can quietly swap it later.

This platform has no memory. countMailable is live, subscriber status counts are live, suppression rows carry only a creation timestamp, and reclassify rewrites open history in place without correcting the legacy columns. Every longitudinal metric in this plan exists only because someone takes a dated snapshot before each stage. That snapshot is the cheapest and most irreversible task in the whole instrumentation list.

Work with the platform's shape rather than against it. Three of the four things a 7-stage cohort campaign normally needs (variants, behavioural segments, journeys) simply do not exist in the code. But arms can be static lists, pacing can be 500-address chunk lists, per-stage reply capture can be per-campaign Reply-To aliases, and stop-the-send can be cancel-schedule on the next chunk. Every one of those is configuration, not code, and each one buys back a measurement that would otherwise be lost while a build waits.

Do the power arithmetic before the test, not after. With 3,027 treated split into two arms of about 1,500, the minimum detectable difference is roughly 3.1 points on a 25% open rate and roughly 1.6 points on a 5% registration rate. That means subject lines are testable on this list and conversion is not. Declaring a body-copy winner from 1,500 per arm is not analysis, it is noise with a headline.

A holdout is the only instrument that answers 'did the emails cause anything'. Everything else measures the behaviour of people who were emailed. 336 people held out costs about 17 registrations and is the difference between reporting activity and reporting effect. Contamination through forwarding shrinks measured lift, so a holdout result is always a conservative floor and should be presented that way.

Deliverability is a leading indicator and analytics is a lagging one. Seed placement and Google Postmaster Tools tell you on day 3 what open rate will tell you on day 10. On a list that is roughly 88% free-mail and gmail-dominant, Postmaster Tools is a more important instrument than anything inside JCF-Mailer, and it is free.

Configuration changes are data changes. Raising analytics.prefetchWindowSeconds and re-running reclassify changes the historical open rate of stages already sent. Any published figure must carry the classifier configuration that produced it, or the campaign's own numbers will contradict each other in the post-mortem and nobody will be able to say which was right.

Every target in this plan is an estimate and should be labelled as one in the report. There is no open rate, click rate, bounce rate, complaint rate or delivery count anywhere on this machine from the June sends, so there is no local baseline to calibrate against. The only hard local data points are the 3,367 addresses emailed, 163 Zoom registrants of whom 128 were on the list, and 309 attendees on 27 June. This campaign's real deliverable is that the next campaign will have a baseline.

Audience discipline is a deliverability control, not just a copy rule. This is a professional clinical list with no seniority or specialty tagging, sent to personal inboxes. Frequency caps (3 per contact per 7 days), a named human sender, a visible NGO registration and consent line, and never sending a Zoom link to a non-registrant are what keep the complaint rate under 0.1%. Copy quality and complaint rate are the same variable measured two different ways.

Warm regards,

Priyanka Joshi
Founder, Jarurat Care Foundation

emails.cta: Nothing to do, unless the new date does not suit you

issues.where: STAGES → pre-flight + Stage 1 ("the fresh horizonevent.info sending domain", "warm-up rung", killCriteria "if GET /api/overview shows DKIM or MAIL FROM unverified on horizonevent.info")
issues.problem: There is no per-campaign sending domain. SesSender.build() always sets .fromEmailAddress() from the single ${aws.ses.fromEmail} (default admin@jarurat.care); Campaign only overrides fromName and replyTo. SafetyCheckService.checkSenderDomain and OverviewApi both call ses.identityHealth(${aws.ses.domain}) — one global value. Tracking, click and unsubscribe URLs come from a third global, ${app.domain} (https://mailer.jarurat.care), so even after switching the From domain every link in a 'horizonevent.info' email points at mailer.jarurat.care, which is a visible domain mismatch and an alignment/reputation problem in its own right.
issues.fix: Treat the domain switch as a platform migration, not a campaign setting: verify horizonevent.info as a new SES identity, set SES_DOMAIN, SES_FROM_EMAIL, SES_REPLY_TO and APP_DOMAIN, add DNS for the tracking host, and restart. Everything the platform sends — including transactional mail via /api/v1/transactional/send — moves with it. If you want jarurat.care transactional mail to stay put, you need a second instance or a per-campaign fromEmail: add `fromEmail` to models/Campaign.java, thread it through SesSender.Outgoing, and make SafetyCheckService.checkSenderDomain resolve the domain from the campaign rather than the property.

issues.where: STAGES → pre-flight ("Run POST /api/verification/list?listId= on C4 and drop UNDELIVERABLE"); Stage 1 killCriteria ("re-verify the remaining cold list instead"); exitRules ("PERMANENT: verification verdict UNDELIVERABLE"); Stage 8b ("zero-engagement and RISKY/catch-all")
issues.problem: Verification cannot see mailbox existence on this box. SmtpProbe is off by default (verification.smtp.enabled:false) and its own header comment states outbound port 25 is blocked by AWS on these instances, so the probe times out on every connect. Without it EmailVerifier returns UNDELIVERABLE only for malformed syntax, NXDOMAIN, null MX, no MX, or a disposable domain. On a 92% free-mail list every gmail.com / yahoo.com address returns DELIVERABLE with reason 'Domain accepts mail, syntax and MX both check out' — including dead accounts. The pre-flight drop will remove almost nothing and buys zero bounce protection on C4. Worse, Stage 8b's suppression criterion (RISKY/catch-all) will select almost exclusively hospital and institutional domains, because those are the ones that come back catch-all or role-account, so the rule suppresses your most valuable contacts and spares the dead Gmails.
issues.fix: Stop treating verification as a bounce gate for free-mail. Keep the run (it still catches dead domains and typos, cheaply) but re-plan the Day 5 gate around the real first-send bounce number, and size batch 1 small enough that its bounce rate is the experiment. Delete the RISKY/catch-all criterion from Stage 8b entirely and sunset on engagement only. If mailbox-level verification actually matters, run it from a machine with unblocked port 25 and disposable IP reputation with verification.smtp.enabled=true — never from the sending box.

issues.where: COHORTS → B9 sqlOrRule ("SELECT r.subscriber_id ... WHERE r.status='FAILED' AND r.sent_at > now() - interval '30 days'")
issues.problem: That query returns zero rows, always. CampaignService.sendOne's catch block sets status='FAILED' and failReason and nothing else — it never calls setSentAt. queueFromList inserts rows with no sent_at. So sent_at IS NULL on every FAILED row and the predicate can never be true. AnalyticsAggregateRepository documents the same fact in its own comment: 'a FAILED or SKIPPED recipient never got a sentAt, so there is no timestamp to filter on'.
issues.fix: Drop the date predicate and window on the campaign set instead: `WHERE r.status='FAILED' AND r.campaign_id IN (:flowStageIds) GROUP BY r.subscriber_id HAVING count(distinct r.campaign_id) >= 2`. For a real timestamp, either add `failedAt` to models/CampaignRecipient.java and set it in the sendOne catch block, or use the message_log arm alone (MessageLogEntry does carry a timestamp and campaignId).

issues.where: STAGES → Stage 5 branch "Bounce or complaint spike on the retry → goesTo: Immediate halt of remaining sends to the cold segment"
issues.problem: There is no way to stop a send in progress. Campaign.status documents PAUSED but nothing in src/ ever writes it (grep confirms the string appears only in that javadoc line). CampaignApi has no pause, abort or stop endpoint; POST /api/campaigns/delete explicitly refuses while status is SENDING. Once CampaignService.dispatchAll is running it drains every PENDING row through 16 concurrent virtual threads at 12/s and cannot be interrupted.
issues.fix: The only halt today is `systemctl restart` on the app — dispatchAll dies, remaining rows stay PENDING, and POST /api/campaigns/send resumes them later (liveRuns is in-memory so the 'already sending' guard is cleared). Write that into the runbook as the emergency stop, with the caveat that campaign.status will be stranded on SENDING. The real fix is small: a volatile `cancelled` flag on Progress, a check at the top of sendOne, and POST /api/campaigns/{id}/abort that sets it. Independently, split every large cold send into ≤600-address lists so the blast radius between checkpoints is bounded — which is what the Stage 1d batching already does and Stage 2/3/5b do not.

issues.where: STAGES → Stage 1 teachingNote ("the 12 blank-first-name rows in horizon-clean.csv would render 'Dear ,'"); A/B → HZN-T7 guardrail ("the 12 blank-first-name rows must be excluded from the personalised arm entirely, because applyMergeFields blanks unresolved tokens")
issues.problem: Half wrong, and the wrong half is the one you built a micro-list and a test guardrail around. CampaignService.firstWord() returns the literal string "there" for a null or blank name (`if (s == null || s.isBlank()) return "there";`), and again when the name is a bare honorific. So {{FIRST_NAME}} on a blank row renders 'Dear there,' — clumsy, not broken. {{NAME}} is the one that renders empty, because queueFromList writes `nullif(trim(first||' '||last),'')` into campaign_recipient.name and applyMergeFields blanks nulls. Separately: TemplateLibraryService.validate() will NOT warn you about any of this, because mergeFieldsOf(subject, html) treats FIRST_NAME and NAME as resolvable CAMPAIGN_FIELDS. The pre-send gate is blind to the exact defect the design names as its top copy risk — a {{FIRST_NAME}} in a subject line passes validation clean and then ships literally, because sendOne passes campaign.getSubject() to SES with no merge pass.
issues.fix: Use {{FIRST_NAME}} and never {{NAME}} in greetings; the micro-list for the 12 blank rows becomes optional rather than mandatory, and HZN-T7's exclusion guardrail is unnecessary. Keep a hard human check that no {{ appears in any subject field — the platform will not catch it. The one-line code fix is worth doing: in CampaignService.sendOne, replace `campaign.getSubject()` with `ses.renderTransactional(campaign.getSubject(), merge)` so subject merge works; then add a validate() rule that flags merge tags in a MARKETING subject until that ships.

issues.where: MEASUREMENT → "Delivery rate", Stage 5 killCriteria ("Do not send 5b if Stage 3's cold cut showed a complaint rate above 0.08%"), Stage 1 Day 5 gate, A/B HZN-T1/T2/T4/T5 guardrails
issues.problem: The attribution heuristic is worse than the design's paraphrase. AnalyticsAggregateRepository.countAttributedSuppressions joins GlobalSuppression to CampaignRecipient on email with `g.timestamp >= r.sentAt` — so every suppression is charged back to every earlier campaign that mailed that address inside the query window. In a 7-stage flow, a person who unsubscribes at Stage 6 raises Stage 1's, 2's and 3's unsubscribeRate retroactively. Per-stage bounce, complaint and unsubscribe rates therefore rise monotonically forever and are not comparable across stages or across time. Reading 'Stage 3's complaint rate' three weeks later gives a different, higher number than reading it at Stage 3+72h.
issues.fix: Read every per-stage rate once, at a fixed offset after that stage's send, and freeze it in your own sheet — never re-read it later and never compare a fresh stage's rate to an aged one. Same-time A/B arm comparisons (HZN-T1 etc.) stay valid because both arms age identically. For the Stage 5b gate specifically, compute complaints directly instead: `SELECT count(*) FROM global_suppression WHERE reason='COMPLAINT' AND timestamp BETWEEN <stage3 send> AND <stage3 send + 72h>` divided by that stage's sent count.

issues.where: STAGES → every branch "Run POST /api/analytics/reclassify before cutting the set" (Stage 1, Stage 2, Day 11 calendar entry)
issues.problem: This is a no-op ritual as written. OpenTrackingService.reclassify re-runs the *same* OpenClassifier over stored rows and rewrites only verdicts that changed. Classification is already computed by that identical classifier at write time in recordOpen/recordClick. Unless analytics.prefetchWindowSeconds or analytics.appleNetworks changed between the send and the reclassify, it will report changed=0 every time. It also does not fix anything: it rewrites tracking_event only and the class's own javadoc states the legacy openedAt/openCount on CampaignRecipient are never retro-corrected.
issues.fix: Drop reclassify from the per-stage runbook. Run it once, deliberately, and only after you change a classifier setting — the realistic case is loading a refreshed Apple egress CIDR list into analytics.appleNetworks (currently only 17.0.0.0/8 is built in, and the code says the leased proxy ranges are NOT baked in). Do that once at pre-flight, before Stage 1, so every stage is classified under the same rules; changing it mid-flow makes stages uncomparable.

issues.where: COHORTS → B4/B5/B6/B7 ("NEEDS: VERP reply-to", "MessageSummary carries no In-Reply-To"); STAGES → Stage 4 measuredHow; A/B → HZN-T6 verdict "skip"
issues.problem: The audit is wrong here and the design inherited the error. MailService.BODY_PROPS requests "messageId", "inReplyTo", "references" from JMAP and MessageBody carries all three (mail/MailService.java getMessage, mail/MessageBody.java). Only MessageSummary lacks them, and MailApiController.message() simply forgets to put them in the JSON. Meanwhile CampaignRecipient.messageId holds the SES messageId, which is the local part of the RFC Message-ID SES stamps (<{id}@{region}.amazonses.com>) — so a reply's In-Reply-To header can be matched straight back to a recipient row with no VERP at all. Second correction: MailCredentialStore is process-wide (InMemoryMailCredentialStore is a ConcurrentHashMap on a @Component), not session-scoped. Only the HTTP layer pins a mailbox to an HttpSession. A @Scheduled bean can call credentials.secretFor("partnership@jarurat.care") directly once any human has unlocked it since the last restart.
issues.fix: The reply build is far cheaper than the design budgets. Step 1 (one line): add `out.put("inReplyTo", body.inReplyTo())` to MailApiController.message() — that alone lets a human paste a message id and get the campaign. Step 2 (small): a ReplyScanner @Scheduled(fixedDelay=300_000) that walks MailService.listMessages on the inbox folder, calls getMessage on unseen rows, strips <…@…> from inReplyTo, and looks up CampaignRecipientRepository by messageId; write campaign_reply(id, campaign_id, recipient_id, subscriber_id, jmap_email_id UNIQUE, intent, received_at). Guard it with `if (credentials.secretFor(mailbox).isEmpty()) return;` and add an ops step 'unlock partnership@ after every app restart'. VERP is a fallback for replies that strip In-Reply-To, not the prerequisite. HZN-T6 should be re-verdicted from 'skip' to 'run it once the scanner ships', which is days not weeks.

issues.where: STAGES → Stage 1d "batch 1 (600), batch 2 (1,100), batch 3 (remainder ~860)"; Stage 8b ("removed from the active list into Horizon-Dormant-2026 via POST /api/subscribers/remove-from-list + add-to-list"); COHORTS → B3 ("campaign N+1 targets a list built as (audience list) MINUS (registrants list)")
issues.problem: None of these list operations exist in the shape assumed. (a) There is no send batching: CampaignService.send calls queueAudience which queues the entire list, then drains it. Three batches means three separate MailingLists and three separate Campaigns. (b) There is no bulk remove: POST /api/subscribers/remove-from-list takes one numeric subscriberId per call, so Stage 8b is ~1,700 individual POSTs plus 1,700 id lookups. (c) There is no set-difference and no in-place rebuild: CSV import only ever ADDS (SubscriberService.importCsv), and MailingList.name is UNIQUE so you cannot recreate a list under the same name without POST /api/lists/delete first — and deleting a list that a campaign points at makes queueAudience throw 'That list no longer exists' and SafetyCheckService raise a LIST_DELETED blocker.
issues.fix: Work in dated, immutable lists, one per stage: 'HZN4-S5b-2026-09-21'. Build each one outside the platform — GET /api/subscribers/export?listId=N&status=SUBSCRIBED gives you the source CSV (the audit missed that this endpoint takes listId and status, not just q), diff it against the Zoom registrant export and your tracking_event pull with a two-line script, then POST /api/campaignsplus/import?listId=<new>&dryRun=true to preview and again with dryRun=false to load. Never delete or mutate a list a campaign has pointed at. For Stage 8b, do not remove anyone: create 'Horizon-Dormant-2026' by import and simply stop targeting the old list.

issues.where: COHORTS → B5 ("adds the address to static list ... via POST /api/subscribers/add-to-list"); B6 (same); B7
issues.problem: POST /api/subscribers/add-to-list takes subscriberId and listId — it does not accept an email address, so a human reading the inbox cannot use it without first looking up the numeric id via GET /api/subscribers?q=<email>. Two calls and a JSON dig per reply, done by hand, during the stage with a 24-hour SLA. That friction is exactly how the manual loop silently stops being run.
issues.fix: Use POST /api/subscribers?email=<addr>&listId=<id> instead. AudienceApi.addSubscriber upserts by lowercased email (SubscriberService.upsert) and attaches to the list in one call, so it is a single curl with the address you already have in front of you. Put that exact command in the runbook for B5/B6.

issues.where: COHORTS → B15 Path A ("give the forwardable share link a distinct URL with ?source=forward, then ... WHERE event_type='CLICK' AND classification='HUMAN' AND url LIKE '%source=forward%'")
issues.problem: "whatsapp" is in OpenClassifier.SCANNER_TOKENS (the link-unfurler group). Any click whose User-Agent contains that substring is classified BOT and excluded from every HUMAN rate. On an Indian clinician list where forwarding happens overwhelmingly through WhatsApp, the single cohort you most want to measure is the one whose traffic is most likely to be classified away. "telegrambot", "slackbot" and "preview" are in the same list. The classifier is right to do this — an unfurl is not a read — but it means B15 Path A systematically undercounts the forward channel rather than measuring it.
issues.fix: Do not judge B15 on HUMAN clicks. Query the ?source=forward URL across ALL classifications and report the split: `SELECT classification, count(*), count(distinct email) FROM tracking_event WHERE event_type='CLICK' AND url LIKE '%source=forward%' GROUP BY classification`. A BOT-classified WhatsApp unfurl still proves the link was pasted into a chat, which is the forward signal you want, even though it is not a read. Path B (Zoom registrant export minus subscriber.email) stays the ground truth and should be the headline number; treat Path A as a directional share-rate indicator only.

issues.where: STAGES → Stage 4 ("plain-text-style, from a named person, short"); A/B → HZN-T4 variantB ("Short: ... one link. No agenda block"), HZN-T6 variantB ("no link in the body")
issues.problem: You cannot send a plain-text campaign. SesSender.build always constructs multipart/alternative with an HTML part plus an auto-derived text part (toPlainText), and renderMarketing then force-appends a bordered grey unsubscribe footer div whenever {{UNSUBSCRIBE_LINK}} is absent, plus a 1x1 tracking pixel div when trackOpens is true. So the 'personal email from a named human' arrives with visible template chrome and an invisible tracker — the two things that break the illusion the stage is buying. HZN-T6's 'no link in the body' arm is also not link-free for the same reason.
issues.fix:
For Stage 4 put {{UNSUBSCRIBE_LINK}} inline inside a plain closing sentence ('If you'd rather not hear about these, unsubscribe here.') so the styled footer is not injected, and keep the HTML body to bare

tags with no table, no width, no colours. Then decide the pixel deliberately: leaving trackOpens=true keeps the stage's 40-50% open metric but embeds a tracker in a peer-to-peer email; setting trackOpens=false makes it honest and makes the 'Opened but did not reply or register' branch unmeasurable, so that branch must fall back to 'did not reply and did not register'. Pick one and write it down — the design currently assumes both.

issues.where: COHORTS → B8/B9 ("NEEDS: jarurat.sns.allowed-topic-arns and aws.ses.configurationSet set"); MEASUREMENT → Delivery rate trap ("Until both are fixed")
issues.problem: Framing this as a config toggle is optimistic. Two independent code comments state the account cannot have an SNS topic at all: TrackingController's deleted-endpoint note says 'This account has no SNS topic and the IAM user cannot create one (SNS:CreateTopic is denied)', and SuppressionService.syncFromSes repeats 'No SNS topic is attached to this AWS account and the instance role cannot create one'. So there is no property value to set until someone with different IAM rights creates the topic and subscribes the endpoint. Everything downstream of that — true soft bounces, deferrals, per-message Delivery events, B9's 'post-acceptance soft bounce' cohort, and MEASUREMENT's per-recipient delivery truth — is blocked on an AWS permissions change, not an application change.
issues.fix: Raise the IAM change as its own pre-flight task with an owner and a date, well before T-30: grant SNS:CreateTopic/Subscribe, create the topic, create an SES configuration set publishing Bounce/Complaint/Delivery to it, set SES_CONFIGURATION_SET and jarurat.sns.allowed-topic-arns, restart. If it will not land in time, delete cohort B9 from this edition entirely rather than carrying it as a rule nobody can evaluate, and state delivery rate as 'SES-accepted, lower bound' everywhere it is reported. There is a partial substitute the design never mentions: messagelog/StalwartDeliveryLog reads this box's own Stalwart log for verbatim SMTP replies — useful for mail sent through Stalwart, not for SES campaign sends.

issues.where: STAGES → every timing claim ("07:10 IST", "21:15 IST", "Minutes are set to :10 because runDueCampaigns polls every 60 seconds"); A/B → HZN-T3 (11:00 vs 20:00 IST)
issues.problem: POST /api/campaigns/schedule?when= does LocalDateTime.parse(when) with no zone, and CampaignService.runDueCampaigns compares against LocalDateTime.now() — both resolve in the JVM's default timezone. Nothing in application.properties sets a timezone. If the box runs UTC (the AWS default for Amazon Linux), '2026-08-31T07:10' fires at 12:40 IST, in the middle of the 11:00-16:00 OPD window the design explicitly forbids sending in. HZN-T3's entire hypothesis is a timezone assertion and would be silently testing 16:30 vs 01:30 IST. Separately, runDueCampaigns has no cross-process lock, so two app instances would both fire a scheduled campaign.
issues.fix: Before anything is scheduled, run `date` on the box and check the JVM zone. Either set TZ=Asia/Kolkata for the service (simplest, and correct given a single-timezone audience), or convert every time in the calendar to the server's zone and put the converted values in the runbook. Verify once by scheduling a test-send two minutes out and checking the arrival timestamp. Confirm only one app instance is running before the flow starts.

issues.where: MEASUREMENT and every "GET /api/analytics/summary?campaignId=X&days=N" read, e.g. Stage 1 Day 5 ("days=2"), Stage 5 ("days=1")
issues.problem: The days window filters BOTH the send (CampaignRecipient.sentAt) and the events (TrackingEvent.timestamp) in AnalyticsService.summary. Two consequences the design does not account for. First, a window that excludes the send day returns sent=0, and CampaignService.rate returns 0 when the denominator is 0 — so every rate silently reports 0.0% instead of erroring. Second, a tight window truncates the open/click tail, which directly contradicts the design's own B14 late-engager finding and its 72h/96h branch waits: `days=2` on a campaign sent 2 days ago discards everything after hour 48. Minor related point: unfilteredOpens sums four per-classification unique counts, so a person with both a HUMAN and an MPP open is counted twice and inflationFactor is overstated.
issues.fix: Always pass days large enough to cover send day through read day inclusive, and standardise on one value per read type: days=7 for a 72h branch cut, days=14 for a 96h cut, days=60 for the whole-flow retrospective. Sanity-check every response by confirming the `sent` key matches the campaign's known recipient count before reading any rate. Report inflationFactor as approximate.

issues.where: COHORTS → B6 whyDifferent ("Do NOT add to global_suppression, because SuppressionService.suppress also flips Subscriber.status and that is effectively irreversible for future campaigns")
issues.problem: The stated code reason is wrong. SuppressionService.unsuppress deletes the global_suppression row AND calls markStatusByEmail(clean, "SUBSCRIBED"), fully reversing both effects, and it is exposed as POST /api/suppressions/remove. The advice not to suppress a 'not now' is still right on consent grounds — but justifying it with a false technical claim means someone will check, find it reversible, and start suppressing people casually. The genuine footgun is the opposite one: unsuppress blindly sets status='SUBSCRIBED' even for an address that was BOUNCED or COMPLAINED, so an over-eager 'remove from suppression' resurrects a hard-bounced address into the mailable pool.
issues.fix: Restate the rule as policy: 'a soft no is not consent withdrawal, so it does not belong in the suppression table' — no code justification needed. Add an operational rule that POST /api/suppressions/remove is only ever used for a MANUAL-reason row, never for BOUNCE or COMPLAINT, and check GET /api/suppressions?reason= before removing anything.

issues.where: STAGES → any stage using POST /api/campaigns/queue ahead of the send (implied by "snapshot the list" workflow), and every scheduled stage
issues.problem: SafetyCheckService.checkSuppression raises SUPPRESSED_QUEUED as a BLOCKER — not a warning — whenever any PENDING row's address is on the suppression list, and assertSafeToSend is called on the caller's thread inside CampaignService.send, so it also gates scheduled fires. In a 43-day flow where people unsubscribe continuously, any campaign queued more than a few hours before its send will hit this and refuse to send, including at 07:10 unattended. The design never mentions the safety check or POST /api/campaignsplus/campaigns/{id}/drop-suppressed.
issues.fix: Do not pre-queue. POST /api/campaigns/send calls queueAudience itself, and queueFromList already excludes suppressed addresses at that moment. If a stage must be queued early (to read the audience size), call POST /api/campaignsplus/campaigns/{id}/drop-suppressed immediately before sending. Add 'GET /api/campaignsplus/campaigns/{id}/safety-check returns passed:true' as a mandatory line item in every stage's pre-send checklist — it is also where you will see the SES 24h quota blocker (QUOTA_EXCEEDED fires when the audience exceeds remaining quota, which a 3,290-recipient Stage 2 plus a 3,150-recipient Stage 3 three days later can trip).

issues.where: STAGES → branches that build set differences from "GET /api/campaigns/{id}/export?status=SENT" (Stage 1, Stage 3, Stage 5b) and MEASUREMENT reads of that CSV
issues.problem: Two traps in that export. First, CampaignApi.export pages with PageRequest.of(page, 500) and the underlying CampaignRecipientRepository.search query has no ORDER BY, so on Postgres the page boundaries are not guaranteed stable across a 3,363-row export — rows can repeat or be skipped. GET /api/subscribers/export has the identical shape. Second, its 'Opens' and 'Clicks' columns are CampaignRecipient.openCount/clickCount, which are the legacy inflated counters, not HUMAN-classified — someone will build a branch on them.
issues.fix: After every export, dedupe by email and assert the row count matches the campaign's `sent` figure from GET /api/analytics/summary before using it. Use the export for the email set only; get all engagement from tracking_event. The code fix is one line each: add Sort.by("id") to both PageRequest.of calls.

issues.where: A/B → HZN-T1/T2 ("reliableOpens / delivered from GET /api/analytics/summary per arm campaign"); STAGES → Stage 3 ("two campaigns because the platform has no variant column")
issues.problem: The design is right that arms must be separate campaigns, but it does not say that Campaign.name is UNIQUE (models/Campaign.java, @Column(nullable=false, unique=true)) and that GET /api/analytics/campaigns compares whole campaigns with no way to collapse two campaigns into one arm. With HZN-T1 crossed against HZN-T2 you get four campaigns at Stage 2, and the 'main effect collapsed across the two sender arms' the design asks for is not computable from any endpoint — you have to sum two campaigns' reliableOpens and delivered by hand, and reliableOpens is a count(distinct email) per campaign so summing is only valid because the arms are disjoint.
issues.fix: Adopt a strict naming scheme up front — HZN4-S2-SND{A|B}-SUB{A|B} — since names are unique and permanent. Record each arm campaign's id at creation. Compute pooled main effects yourself: sum reliableOpens and sum delivered across the two campaigns in the level (valid only because arm membership is disjoint by construction), and state in the pre-registration that this hand-summing is the method. Do not use GET /api/analytics/campaigns for anything but a sanity check.

issues.where: exitRules → "PERMANENT: verification verdict UNDELIVERABLE ... Re-verification is allowed only if the address was checked more than 180 days ago"
issues.problem: The platform's freshness window is 90 days (verification.freshDays:90 in VerificationService), not 180, and POST /api/verification/list takes a `force` parameter the design does not mention that overrides it entirely. A verification run at pre-flight will silently re-check anything older than 90 days and skip anything newer, regardless of the stated 180-day policy.
issues.fix: Either state 90 to match the platform, or set verification.freshDays=180 in application.properties so the code enforces the policy. Note that `force=true` bypasses it, and keep that flag out of the runbook.

issues.where: Whole package - the email index
issues.problem: There is no email index. The playbook specifies 20 individual sends (S1a-d x3 batches, S2, S3 warm/cold, S4 + peer cut, S5a, S5b, S6a, S6b, day-of 09:00, day-of 18:00, S7a/b/c, S8a) and contains zero subject lines and zero bodies for 18 of them. The only copy anywhere is two A/B subject variants for a stage whose definition is itself contradicted, and one fragment. A junior cannot execute a single send from this document.
issues.fix: Before anything ships, produce an email index table: send ID, cohort, audience rule, send datetime, subject, preheader, from/replyTo, body owner, copy-freeze date, asset dependencies, approver. Nothing gets a calendar slot until it has a row. Every cohort B1-B15 must map to at least one send ID or be explicitly marked 'no email by design'.

issues.where: STAGES calendar vs A/B test plan (HZN-T0 through HZN-T7)
issues.problem: The two documents describe different campaigns. The calendar is 8 stages over 43 days with Stage 2 = the give (T-14), Stage 3 = registration opens (T-11), Stage 4 = reply loop (T-9). The A/B plan is a 6-stage flow with Stage 1 = Save the Date (T-21), Stage 2 = Registration Open (T-14), Stage 3 = Academic value (T-9), Stage 4 = Final reminder (T-4), Stage 5 = day-of. HZN-T2 therefore tests a faculty/registration subject line on 'Stage 2', which the calendar's own kill criteria forbid ('do not sneak a registration CTA in, not even in the footer'). HZN-T0 says the holdout is 'held for all 6 stages'. A junior building from the A/B plan builds the wrong campaigns.
issues.fix: Pick one canonical stage numbering, renumber the A/B plan onto it, and re-derive every T-offset. Then re-check each test's stage assignment against that stage's purpose - T2's subject contrast belongs on the ask (calendar Stage 3), not on the give.
