issues.where: HZN-T0 holdout vs every audience count in STAGES
issues.problem: The holdout removes 340 people (3,363 - 340 = 3,023 mailable). No stage audience reflects this: Stage 2 targets '~3,290', Stage 3 '~3,150', Stage 1 C4 '2,560-2,960' with C1-C3 on top summing back to the full roster. Executed as written, the flow mails the holdout on Stage 1 and the incrementality test - the only measurement in the package that answers 'does email work at all' - is destroyed on day one, silently.
issues.fix: Subtract the holdout at pre-flight, before the C1-C4 lists are built, and restate every audience number against 3,023. Add a hard pre-send check: diff every import CSV against holdout.csv and abort on any intersection. Also stratify the holdout within cohort (see separate finding) rather than hashing the raw roster.

issues.where: Cohort model, pre-flight, and every send - audience composition
issues.problem: The list is treated as uniformly clinical ('your Monday clinic', 'your subspecialty', CME certificates, 'Dear Colleague') but there is no role field anywhere: no CLINICIAN / CAREGIVER / PATIENT / BEREAVED / UNKNOWN tag, no clinician verification, no exclusion of the foundation's own patient-support contacts. On a cancer NGO's list assembled partly from scraped and 'cold pipeline' sources, patients, caregivers and bereaved families are certainly present. Every one of the 20 sends reaches them, mis-addressed as doctors, with gastric/GE-junction cancer survival content.
issues.fix: Add role classification to pre-flight as a gating step, not a nice-to-have. Anything traceable to patient-support intake is excluded from this programme outright. UNKNOWN-role rows get a restricted track: no diagnosis term in the subject line, no retry send (5b), no sunset email, no forwarding of registrant data into the next edition's warm cohort. Publish the count of each role class before the first send; if UNKNOWN is more than ~20% of the roster, the list is not fit to mail as a clinician list.

issues.where: COHORTS B4-B7 reply intents; exitRules; suppression reasons
issues.problem: The reply intent enum is INTERESTED / QUESTION / NOT_NOW / OPT_OUT and the suppression reasons are UNSUBSCRIBED / BOUNCE / COMPLAINT / MANUAL. There is no category for 'he died in March', 'please remove my late wife's address', or a caregiver replying in grief. On this list that reply will arrive. As written, the reply owner has no instruction, no route, and the address stays mailable into Stage 5b, Stage 6a, the day-of nudge and the Stage 8 sunset email.
issues.fix: Add intent='BEREAVED' ranked ABOVE OPT_OUT in the precedence rules, suppress with reason='BEREAVEMENT' immediately across all JCF programmes (not just this event), and write the single-sentence human acknowledgement into the reply playbook now, before Stage 1. Same-day action, no template that reads like marketing, no further contact ever without an inbound request. Add the same handling for a bounce or reply on an address the attendee log shows registered but never attended.

issues.where: Stage 4 reply loop, Stage 1 reply branch, B5/B7 duties
issues.problem: The reply path is unstaffed on paper. The flow demands 09:00 and 18:00 inbox checks every working day from Day 1 to E+10 (~40 days), a 24h SLA, a sub-4h SLA for partnership replies, weekend replies by Monday 11:00, daily 09:00 Zoom registrant exports, twice-daily during the close window, and a Zoom export within 2h of a Saturday 21:30 event finish. No person is named for any of it. The kill criterion says 'do not send if fewer than two people can hold the 24h SLA' without naming the two, a backup, an escalation path, or who decides. Worse, MailboxAccess keeps the mailbox secret in a browser HttpSession, so exactly one logged-in human can read the inbox at all, and HZN-T1 splits replyTo across two mailboxes (partnership@ and priyanka@), directly contradicting Stage 1's instruction to 'set Campaign.replyTo to a single monitored address so replies do not scatter'.
issues.fix: Publish a rota with named primary and backup per week, an inbound-volume estimate (S4 alone forecasts 15-27 replies; a 3,000-address cold blast adds auto-replies and wrong-address noise - budget 100-200 inbound over the flow), a shared credential out of the browser session, and a single monitored replyTo for the whole flow. If HZN-T1 must vary replyTo, both arm addresses forward into one triaged mailbox. Add a 'do not give medical advice' rule with a named clinician escalation for any patient-origin question - the marketing team must never answer one.

issues.where: Every stage branch; silence counter; Stage 1/2/3 'measuredHow'
issues.problem: Each branch cut is a raw psql query on the Postgres box at mailer.jarurat.care because no endpoint returns the HUMAN-classified set. No scripts are provided, no connection instructions, no export-to-CSV step, no import runbook. The silence counter that gates Stage 5b, Stage 6a and Stage 8 lives 'in your own sheet' - a sheet that does not exist, with no schema and no owner. Rebuilding the target list before every stage is described as a manual CSV MINUS across 3,363 rows, twice a week for six weeks.
issues.fix: Ship, before Monday: six named .sql files (one per branch cut), a one-command wrapper that writes an import-ready CSV, a template silence-counter sheet with a named owner and an update step in every stage's checklist, and a deterministic rebuild script for the audience-MINUS-registrants operation. A junior marketer should never be asked to write a NOT EXISTS join under time pressure the morning of a send.

issues.where: Timing - Stage 3 (Tue 15 Sep), Stage 4 (17 Sep), Stage 5a (19 Sep), Stage 5b (21 Sep), Stage 6a (23 Sep)
issues.problem: No festival or holiday check exists anywhere in the playbook. Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 falls on Monday 14 September and runs ten days to Anant Chaturdashi / Ganesh Visarjan on approximately 23 September. For a Mumbai-run programme this means the single most important send in the flow - Stage 3, the primary registration ask - lands on day two of a Maharashtra public holiday, and Stage 6a, the last-chance email, lands on Visarjan day, when Mumbai effectively shuts down. The entire ask-to-close sequence sits inside the festival.
issues.fix: Shift the ask window. Either pull Stage 3 forward to Tue 8 or Wed 9 September (before the festival) and compress the back half, or move the whole edition's event date. Add a standing pre-flight step: overlay the send calendar against national and Maharashtra/regional holiday calendars and the exam/conference calendar for the specialty before any date is fixed.

issues.where: Timing - post-event sends: Stage 7a/7b (27 Sep), 7c (29 Sep), Stage 8a (5 Oct)
issues.problem: Pitru Paksha in 2026 runs approximately 25 September to 10 October (it ends on Mahalaya Amavasya, the day before Navaratri begins on 11 October). That is a sixteen-day mourning observance of rites for the dead. Every post-event send, including the Stage 8a 'keep me or remove me' sunset email, falls inside it, on a cancer foundation's list that contains bereaved families. This is the highest-risk collision in the calendar and the playbook does not mention it.
issues.fix: Verify the exact 2026 dates against a regional panchang, then move Stage 8a out of the window entirely (it has no deadline - run it at E+21). Keep 7a/7b (certificate and recording are service, not solicitation) but strip any celebratory framing. Add Pitru Paksha and the equivalent regional mourning periods to the standing calendar overlay.

issues.where: Stage 2 (Sat 12 Sep 11:00 IST) and Stage 5a (Sat 19 Sep 11:00 IST) vs Stage 1's own quiet-hours rule
issues.problem: Stage 1 states 'Nothing sends between 11:00 and 16:00 IST (OPD and theatre)'. Two stages then send at exactly 11:00 IST. The justification - 'Saturday late morning is the only unhurried reading window this audience reliably has' - is asserted with no evidence and is wrong for most Indian hospitals, where Saturday is a working OPD day. The flow's two longest-form emails are scheduled into a slot the flow itself declared dead.
issues.fix: Either delete the quiet-hours rule or honour it. If the Saturday hypothesis is worth keeping, test it: send Stage 2 at 08:30 to half and 11:00 to half and read the difference, rather than building two stages on an untested assumption. Sunday 09:00-10:00 is the more defensible 'unhurried' slot for this audience and should be the default candidate.

issues.where: exitRules FREQUENCY-CAP PARK vs the registrant logistics track
issues.problem: The cap parks anyone with three or more sends in a rolling seven days. A registrant receives 6b (24 Sep), day-of 09:00 (26 Sep), day-of 18:00 nudge (26 Sep) and 7a (27 Sep) - four sends in four days. Applied literally, the cap drops registrants out of the T-90-minute join nudge, which the playbook itself calls the fix for the dominant no-show cause. There is no stated exemption.
issues.fix: Write the exemption explicitly: the frequency cap applies to acquisition sends only and never to registrant logistics (6b, day-of, join link, certificate). State it in the exitRules entry, not in someone's head.

issues.where: exitRules unsubscribe enforcement vs the registrant track
issues.problem: Unsubscribe writes global_suppression and is enforced at queue time, send time and suppression time. A registrant who unsubscribes at Stage 3 or 5 therefore never receives 6b, the day-of join link, or the certificate at 7a. They paid the registration with their attention and get silence. Nothing in the playbook flags this, and it will read to the recipient as the foundation losing their registration.
issues.fix: Deliver join link, calendar file and certificate through Zoom's own transactional mail, never through JCF-Mailer. State the rule once, hard: JCF-Mailer carries acquisition only; anything a registrant is owed goes via Zoom. Then add a pre-send check on 6b and the day-of sends that reports how many registrants are suppressed, so the number is visible rather than invisible.

issues.where: B11 (Machine-Open Only) vs Stage 5b, Stage 6a and Stage 8b
issues.problem: B11 argues at length that machine opens must never be treated as disengagement and that MPP-only people must stay in the flow. The stage machinery does the opposite: 'no HUMAN open' increments the silence counter, four counts routes to the Stage 8 sunset pool, Stage 6a explicitly excludes anyone with zero HUMAN opens, and Stage 8b sends zero-engagement plus RISKY addresses to permanent suppression. An iPhone-owning consultant who reads every email is on a path to permanent suppression. The exitRules fatigue definition ('zero tracking_event rows of ANY classification') and the calendar's Day 36 audience ('zero-HUMAN-engagement contacts') are also two different populations.
issues.fix: Fix the definition in one place: the sunset pool is zero tracking_event rows of any classification, full stop. Anyone with APPLE_MPP/PROXY/BOT events is not silent and never enters the sunset or suppression path. Re-cut Stage 6a's exclusion on the same basis, and publish the MPP-only headcount at every stage so the cost of the rule is visible.

issues.where: B13 (Serial Opener, Never Converts) vs Stages 5a, 6a, 7c
issues.problem: B13's prescribed treatment is 'drop them to one email per event' and sell the recording rather than the live seat. The stage machinery sends them Stage 5a (S3 openers who did not click), Stage 6a (any HUMAN open, unregistered) and Stage 7c (engaged never-registered) - the exact opposite. The cohort doctrine and the calendar contradict each other and only the calendar is executable.
issues.fix: Either implement B13 as a real exclusion (a persistent flag, applied at 5a/6a list build, capping them at one send per edition) or delete B13's prescription and admit the flow does not act on it. A cohort with no enforceable exclusion rule is decoration.

issues.where: B2 (Clicked, Not Registered) vs the send calendar
issues.problem: B2 is named the highest-intent non-converter in the flow and its prescribed treatment is specific: a 40-word email with the direct registration link, one line naming the drop-off cause, and an explicit instruction never to put them back in the education track. No such email exists in the calendar. The clicked-not-registered set is routed to Stage 4 (a plain-text reply-ask, a different email doing a different job) and to Stage 6a. The friction email is orphaned.
issues.fix: Add it as its own send at T-10 or T-8: audience = HUMAN click on the registration URL minus the Zoom registrant export, 40 words, one link, distinct UTM. It is the cheapest send in the whole flow and it targets the group most likely to convert.

issues.where: Stage 5a and Stage 5b audience definitions
issues.problem: 5a is 'Stage 3 openers who did not click'. 5b is 'no HUMAN open on Stage 2 or Stage 3'. Anyone who opened Stage 2, was silent on Stage 3, and never clicked falls in neither - they receive no Stage 5 email at all and reappear unexplained at Stage 6a. Given Stage 2's own 18-24% open target on ~3,290, this orphan is several hundred people.
issues.fix: Redefine 5a as 'any HUMAN open on Stage 2 or Stage 3, no HUMAN click' so the two audiences are complementary and exhaustive against the non-registrant pool. Then re-derive both headcounts - 5a's stated 430 does not reconcile with Stage 3's own targets, which imply 500-700 openers-no-click before Stage 2 openers are added.

issues.where: Event day, 18:00 IST T-90 nudge
issues.problem: The registrant export is pulled at 09:00 on 24 Sep for 6b and at 09:00 on event day for the morning reminder. Nothing instructs anyone to re-pull it before the 18:00 nudge. Off-list word of mouth is, by the playbook's own June data, the dominant acquisition channel (191 of 209 attendees) and it peaks on the day. Same-day registrants therefore receive no join reminder at the one moment the playbook says no-shows are actually lost.
issues.fix: Add a mandatory registrant re-pull at 16:30 IST on event day, with the 18:00 nudge list built from it. Name the owner in the runbook.

issues.where: Stage 6 - 'registration closes Fri 25 Sep 18:00 IST'
issues.problem: The deadline is either fake, which violates the stage's own kill criterion ('do not use a fake deadline'), or it is real, in which case it closes the door on the channel that delivered 191 of 209 attendees last time. Free-webinar word of mouth peaks in the final 24 hours and on the day. The flow is optimising urgency at the direct cost of its best-performing acquisition path.
issues.fix: Keep registration open through the event and move the urgency device to something genuinely finite: the calendar hold goes out Friday, the agenda drops Friday, Q&A questions submitted by Friday get answered live. Say exactly that in the copy.

issues.where: B5 reply knowledge base vs Stage 7a/7b
issues.problem: B5 instructs the reply owner to answer that there is a 'Certificate of Participation for all registrants'. Stage 7a sends the certificate to attendees from the Zoom attendee log; 7b (registered no-shows) gets the recording and no certificate. The reply script therefore makes a promise the flow breaks for 150-200 people, and it will generate inbound at exactly the moment the team is least staffed.
issues.fix: Decide the rule now - attendees only, or attendees above a minimum watch time - and write the identical wording into the reply KB, the Stage 3 body, the Stage 6b body and 7a/7b. If no-shows do get a certificate, that must be in 7b.

issues.where: Stage 1 gates vs Day 5 gate vs HZN-T1 guardrail
issues.problem: Three different bounce thresholds govern the same decision: Stage 1 kill criteria say halt above 4% bounce / 0.08% complaint, the Day 5 gate says pass below 4% / 0.08%, HZN-T1's guardrail says both arms must stay below 2.00% bounce and 0.100% complaint, and SafetyCheckService blocks at 5.0%/0.5%. A junior reading a 2.6% bounce on batch 1 does not know whether to fire batch 2.
issues.fix: One table, one owner: metric, threshold, who reads it, what happens above it. Delete the others. Given the Gmail bulk-sender line, set the operational gate at 2% bounce / 0.08% complaint and state that SafetyCheckService's 5.0%/0.5% is a backstop, never a target.

issues.where: Stage 1 domain warm-up on horizonevent.info
issues.problem: The warm-up is a burst, not a ramp: 230, 170, 400, 600, 1,100, 860 across ten days, then three dark days, then 3,290 in one send on 12 Sep - a 3x jump over the largest prior send, on a domain with under two weeks of history. Warm-up also depends on C3 existing, which the playbook admits may not ('if the Postmark export cannot be pulled, this cohort folds into C4'), which silently changes the ramp shape. And the only gate reads bounce on the cold batch; the first three sends (800 emails) generate no gate at all. Separately, DMARC and RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe are never mentioned, only DKIM and MAIL FROM.
issues.fix: Split Stage 2 into two sends 48h apart so nothing more than doubles the previous peak. Add a gate after C1+C2 land, not only after the first cold batch. Resolve the C3 dependency at pre-flight with a hard yes/no date. Add DMARC (at minimum p=none with rua) and List-Unsubscribe-Post one-click to the pre-flight checklist alongside DKIM - Gmail and Yahoo bulk rules require them and the flow's whole complaint anxiety is downstream of that.

issues.where: B15 off-list arrivals; Stage 3/6 registrant CSV import; Stage 7a promotion
issues.problem: Zoom registrants who are not subscribers are imported into JCF-Mailer lists and then mailed, and 7a/7b members are promoted into the next edition's C1 warm cohort. B15 itself says consent capture is needed because a Zoom registration for one event is not blanket marketing consent under DPDP. No consent step exists anywhere in the calendar or the pre-flight. This is also the path by which a patient or family member forwarded the invite enters a clinician marketing list permanently.
issues.fix: Add a consent checkbox to the Zoom registration form (event logistics only vs future invitations) and import only the opt-in column into any marketing list. Registrants without the opt-in receive logistics via Zoom and nothing else, and are never promoted to C1. Record consent source and timestamp per row.

issues.where: Stage 5b - the weakest stage in the flow
issues.problem: 5b mails 2,300 verified non-openers, four days before the close, immediately before Stage 6a which the playbook calls the second-largest registration driver. Its own success criteria concede the point: combined 5a+5b registrations are 20-35 and 5a (430 proven openers at 6-9% click) plausibly supplies most of it, and the stage's stated pass condition is a complaint rate, with the author writing that it 'matters more than the registrations'. So the flow spends its largest single reputation risk to buy perhaps 5-15 registrations, and if it trips SafetyCheckService it blocks Stage 6a's 60-100. It is also where B11's MPP-only readers get pushed toward the sunset pool.
issues.fix: Cut 5b and reuse the slot for a forward kit: send to the ~600 people with any HUMAN engagement, ask each to forward to one colleague, and give the share link a distinct ?source=forward URL so B15 Path A finally produces a number. Zero incremental reputation risk (engaged recipients only) and it attacks the channel the playbook's own data says delivered 191 of 209 attendees while email delivered 18. If leadership insists on a non-opener retry, cap it at the highest-quality domains, exclude every UNKNOWN-role row, and run it after the event as a recording offer, not before the close as another ask.

issues.where: Stage numbering - Stages 1, 5, 6, 7 and 8
issues.problem: The eight-stage framing is a presentation artefact. Stage 1 is six sends to four cohorts plus a warm-up ramp. Stage 5 is two unrelated emails answering two unrelated failure modes. Stage 6 explicitly bundles 'two completely different jobs' by the playbook's own words. Stage 7 is a three-way fork. Stage 8 is list hygiene, not a campaign stage. Meanwhile the platform's own model is one campaign row per send. A junior asked to 'schedule Stage 5' cannot, because Stage 5 is not a thing that can be scheduled.
issues.fix: Renumber by send (S01...S20) as the operational unit, and keep the stage names only as narrative grouping in the strategy summary. Every runbook line, every list name and every A/B arm references a send ID.

issues.where: HZN-T0 holdout construction and HZN-T1 split
issues.problem: The holdout is an unstratified 10% hash of the full roster, so it draws roughly 23 of the ~230 prior attendees - the highest-value registrations in the file - and leaves arm cohort mix to chance, confounding the incrementality read with cohort composition. HZN-T1's observed split of 1,744/1,619 is a 2.2 sigma deviation from an even SHA-256 mod 2 (two-sided p about 0.03), which is unlikely enough to suggest a normalisation bug (case, whitespace, or duplicate handling) rather than luck, and the playbook waves it away on power grounds without checking whether the imbalance correlates with domain.
issues.fix: Stratify both splits within cohort (and within free-mail vs institutional domain), exclude C1 attendees from the holdout entirely, and re-run the hash on normalised lowercased trimmed addresses with the resulting per-domain cross-tab printed before the split is accepted.

issues.where: HZN-T2 decision rule
issues.problem: The primary metric is chosen after reading GET /api/analytics/classifier to compute m from the same programme's data. Choosing the endpoint on the basis of an observed statistic is not pre-registration, however carefully the branch is written down in advance.
issues.fix: Pre-commit to click rate as HZN-T2's primary metric unconditionally and report the open difference as secondary with its CI. The MPP share is already known to be large enough to matter; there is no reason to make the decision conditional.

issues.where: Roster facts across the three documents
issues.problem: Free-mail share is 88% in the stages and measurement documents and 92.1% 'recomputed from the file' in the A/B document. The cohort document references a '12 June' session and 'reg-2026-XX-registrants' placeholders while the calendar uses 27 June and 26 September. The 12 blank-first-name rows get a fifth micro-list at pre-flight and are never mentioned again in any stage audience. Stage 4's audience (~450) is numerically identical to Stage 3's warm cut (~450) despite Stage 3 being expected to convert 90-140 people out of it.
issues.fix: One facts block at the top of the package, recomputed from horizon-clean.csv, cited by every document. Strip placeholder debris. Give the blank-name micro-list an explicit path through every stage or fold it in with a no-name variant flag on the row. Re-derive Stage 4's headcount from Stage 3's own conversion assumptions.

issues.where: Contingency and incident handling
issues.problem: There is no correction procedure for a bad link or wrong date after a 3,000-person send, no cancellation plan beyond one line about the 18:00 nudge, and no contingency if faculty drop at T-9, which would invalidate Stages 4, 5a, 6a and 6b copy simultaneously. Faculty confirmation 'in writing' is a Stage 3 kill criterion with no owner and no deadline in the pre-flight.
issues.fix: Add a faculty-lock date at T-21 with a named owner, a drafted cancellation/substitution email held ready from T-14, and a one-page incident rule: what triggers a correction send, who approves it inside 30 minutes, and the standing template.

issues.where: Post-event operations, Sat 26 Sep 21:30 to Sun 27 Sep 10:30
issues.problem: Zoom exports must be pulled 'within 2 hours of the event ending' - roughly 23:30 on a Saturday night - then cross-matched, imported and two campaigns built and scheduled for 10:00 and 10:30 Sunday. This is unnamed weekend labour on the tightest turnaround in the flow, immediately after a two-hour live event.
issues.fix: Move 7a/7b to Monday 07:10, or pre-build both campaigns on Friday with the audience import as the only Sunday-morning action and a named owner rostered for it. The certificate is not more valuable at Sunday 10:00 than Monday 07:10.

issues.where: Measurement - the scoreboard
issues.problem: The package carries a gross registration target (220-300), an attendance target (100-155) and an incrementality read from HZN-T0 whose decision rule says incremental registrations must become the denominator for every future claim. Nobody states which number the programme is judged on, so the flow will be reported on gross registrations and measured on incremental ones by two different people.
issues.fix: Name one primary: incremental registrations versus holdout, with gross registrations and attendance as supporting lines. Write the reporting template now, with the exact endpoints and the banned legacy ones, so the E+16 publish is a fill-in exercise.

issues.where: COHORTS B15 vs A/B HZN-T0 vs STAGES stage 3 successMetric — the June baseline
issues.problem: The four documents state three mutually exclusive versions of the June run. B15: 209 unique attendees, 18 on the 3,363 list, 191 off-list. HZN-T0: 163 registrants, 35 off-list, so 128 on-list. Those cannot both be true: 128 on-list registrants producing 18 on-list attendees is a 14% show rate, while 35 off-list registrants producing 191 off-list attendees is a 546% show rate. Every downstream target is anchored to whichever of these you believe.
issues.fix: Stop quoting either until the two exports are re-joined on lowercased email. The honest sentence: 'We have one Zoom attendee log (209 rows) and one registrant snapshot (163 rows) that have never been reconciled to each other or to horizon-clean.csv. Until that reconciliation is done we have no baseline registration rate, and no target in this plan should be presented as a multiple of one.'

issues.where: STAGES pre-flight / stage 1 audience — C1 approx 230, C2 approx 170
issues.problem: Both numbers are impossible against the plan's own evidence. C1 is defined as attendees 'deduped and matched to the list', and B15 says only 18 attendees appear on the list — so C1 is 18, not 230. C2 is 'registrant export minus attendee log' and there were only 163 registrants in total, so C2 cannot be 170 no matter how few attended. The 230/170 figures appear to come from building C1/C2 out of the raw Zoom exports, i.e. mailing people who are not subscribers at all.
issues.fix: Replace with the measured values: C1 = 18 matched attendees (plus up to 191 unmatched attendee addresses that are NOT mailable without consent capture), C2 = 163 minus whatever attended, hard-capped at 163. If C1 is really 18, the whole 'smallest, warmest cohort first' warm-up rung collapses and the ramp must be redesigned.

issues.where: COHORTS B15 ('NEEDS: consent capture before adding them, since a Zoom registration for one event is not blanket marketing consent under the DPDP framing') vs STAGES pre-flight (POST /api/lists/import of the attendee and registrant CSVs)
issues.problem: The plan states the consent rule and then breaks it in the very first operational step. It also never applies the same test to the base list, which the MEASUREMENT doc calls a '2026-recut scraped list' and COHORTS B10 calls 'cold or scraped provenance'. Under DPDP 2023 the scraped 2,560-2,960 cold addresses are the larger exposure, not the Zoom registrants, yet consent is only raised for the Zoom side.
issues.fix: Add a pre-flight legal gate: 'We cannot document lawful basis for the ~2,900 scraped rows or for the 191 off-list attendee addresses. Either produce per-row provenance and consent evidence before Stage 1, or run Stage 1 only against rows with documented opt-in and treat the rest as a separate, disclosed risk decision signed off by the founder.' This is a go/no-go item, not a footnote.

issues.where: A/B HZN-T0 (340-person holdout) vs STAGES calendar and every stage audience
issues.problem: The A/B plan carves out 340 people who receive zero email, leaving 3,023 mailable. The send calendar never mentions the holdout: pre-flight builds C1-C4 to cover the whole 3,363, Stage 2 mails ~3,290, Stage 3 ~3,150. The holdout would be mailed at Stage 1 and the incrementality test destroyed before it starts. It is also unclear whether Stage 8's sunset list includes the never-mailed 340, who would show zero engagement by construction.
issues.fix: Either drop HZN-T0 or subtract 340 from every audience figure in the calendar and add a hard pre-flight exclusion list. Corrected chain: 3,363 roster - (verification drop) - 340 holdout = mailable. Also exclude the holdout from Stage 8 sunset scoring explicitly, or you will suppress 340 people for silence you engineered.

issues.where: MEASUREMENT ('Treat anything above 40% as a classifier problem, not a copy win'; stage 1 HUMAN open 20-30%, day-of 25-35%) vs STAGES success metrics
issues.problem: The stage targets sit above the plan's own classifier ceiling: Stage 1 C1 '45-55%', Stage 4 '40-50%', Stage 6b '55-70%', day-of '50-65%', 18:00 nudge '45-60%'. By the measurement doc's rule these are not targets, they are the definition of a broken classifier. None cite a source or a prior Horizon edition.
issues.fix: Cap every HUMAN-open target at the measurement doc's own bands and mark them ESTIMATE: warm/registrant sends 25-35%, mid-flow 14-22%, cold first touch 12-18%. Replacement sentence: 'No Horizon edition has ever produced a classified HUMAN open rate, so all open targets below are priors, not forecasts, and the first stage's actual number replaces them.'

issues.where: STAGES flowSummary and stage 4 successMetric — 'a reply converts at roughly ten times the rate of a click'
issues.problem: Pure fabrication. COHORTS B4 says replies are 'completely invisible to the platform', stage 4 says there is no reply detection, no REPLIED status, no VERP, and HZN-T6 says 'Reply count is NOT available as a metric'. There is no dataset anywhere in this plan from which a 10x figure could have been computed, yet it is used to justify the existence of Stage 4 and its staffing cost.
issues.fix: Delete the multiplier. Replacement: 'We believe replies convert better than clicks and have no measurement to support any specific ratio. Stage 4 is funded as a bet, and the first thing it produces is the baseline reply rate, not a confirmation of one.' Same treatment for the unsourced '3-5x lift' claimed for the peer-to-peer clinician send in stage 4 killCriteria.

issues.where: A/B HZN-T1 sampleSizeMath — 'Need 2,748 delivered, have 2,842. FITS with 3% headroom'
issues.problem: The chain 3,363 -> 3,023 -> 2,842 never subtracts the pre-flight verification drop that the plan itself schedules ('Run POST /api/verification/list on C4 and drop UNDELIVERABLE'). On a scraped list last touched two months ago, a 5% UNDELIVERABLE rate is conservative. Redoing it: 3,363 x 0.95 = 3,195; minus 340 holdout = 2,855; x 0.94 delivered = 2,684; = 1,342 per arm against 1,374 required. The 3% headroom is already spent, and that is before the arms' actual 1,744/1,619 imbalance. The verdict 'run-it' is not supported.
issues.fix: Change the verdict to 'run-it, underpowered, read as directional'. Honest sentence: 'At a realistic 2,650-2,750 delivered we are at or just under the 1,374/arm needed for a 5pt MDE, so a null result means nothing and only a difference above roughly 5pt is interpretable.' Alternatively drop HZN-T0's holdout to recover the 340 and restore power — you cannot afford both tests on this list.

issues.where: Across all three documents — stage numbering, stage count and timeline
issues.problem: COHORTS references 'S1 (Save the Date, T-21)' and 'S2 (Registration Open, T-14)' through S4/S5b. STAGES describes 8 stages over 43 days starting T-26 with Stage 2 as a no-ask give and Stage 3 as the ask at T-11. A/B references 6 stages with Stage 2 = Registration Open T-14, Stage 3 = Academic value T-9, Stage 4 = Final reminder T-4, Stage 5 = day-of. Every branch rule, cohort trigger and test assignment keyed to 'Stage 3' is therefore ambiguous, and HZN-T3's 'Tuesday 11:00 IST' arm also violates the calendar's own 'nothing sends between 11:00 and 16:00 IST' rule.
issues.fix: Freeze one canonical stage table (number, date, time, audience, campaign id) and rewrite the cohort and A/B docs against it before anything is scheduled. Until that exists, no branch rule in this plan is executable by a second person.

issues.where: STAGES stage 6 successMetric — 'Whole-flow target: 220-300 list-attributable registrations against a roughly 163 baseline'
issues.problem: Three defects in one sentence. (1) 163 is the total registrant count including 35 off-list, so the list-attributable baseline is 128, not 163. (2) 220-300 against 3,023 mailed is a 7.3-9.9% registration rate, i.e. 1.7-2.3x the only observed number, justified by nothing but the existence of more stages. (3) It contradicts HZN-T0's own sample-size assumption of a 5.0% mailed registration rate and HZN-T0's guardrail of 6%.
issues.fix: State the baseline as 128 list-attributable registrations (3.8% of 3,367). Set the target at 4.5-6.0% of mailable, i.e. 135-180 registrations, framed as 'a 20-45% improvement on June'. If you want 220-300, say plainly that it requires a doubling of registration rate that no evidence in these documents supports.

issues.where: STAGES stage 3 teachingNote — 'At roughly 1,300 per arm on a 16% base, the smallest difference you can honestly detect is about 3 percentage points'
issues.problem: Wrong twice. Redoing it with the plan's own formula (7.849 x [p1(1-p1)+p2(1-p2)]/d^2): detecting 16% -> 19% needs 2,514 per arm, not 1,300. At 1,300 per arm on a 16% base the achievable MDE is about 4.2pt, not 3pt — a 40% understatement. Separately, the stage does not have two 1,300-person arms: it splits WARM ~450 / COLD ~2,700, so the sentence describes a test that is not being run.
issues.fix: Replace with: 'The Stage 3 cut is 450 warm vs 2,700 cold, which is a copy cut for relevance, not a test — the arms differ by audience as well as copy, so no comparison between them is interpretable. If you ever run a true 50/50 subject test at this stage, roughly 1,350 per arm on a 16% base detects about 4.2pt and nothing smaller.'

issues.where: A/B — every 'complaint rate <0.100% per arm' guardrail (T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6, T7) and STAGES Day 5 gate 'complaint <0.08%', stage 1 'complaint under 0.05%'
issues.problem: These thresholds are below the resolution of the samples they are applied to. At 1,421 per arm, one complaint = 0.070% and two = 0.141%, so the guardrail flips on a single click of the spam button. On the Day 5 gate the batch is 600, where 0.08% is 0.48 complaints — one complaint (0.167%) fails the gate automatically. On C1's 230-person send, 0.05% is 0.115 complaints. Worse, per the MEASUREMENT doc the SNS webhook 403s on every payload and aws.ses.configurationSet is blank, so per-message complaint events do not exist at all; complaintRate comes from the same over-counting heuristic at AnalyticsAggregateRepository.java:64-83.
issues.fix: Convert every complaint gate to absolute counts and say why: 'Complaint rate is not measurable below roughly 1,000 recipients, and per-arm complaint attribution does not exist until SNS is wired. Gate on counts: halt if batch 1 (600) produces 2 or more complaints or 25 or more bounces; monitor the account-level SES rate weekly against Google's 0.10% line.' The same applies to HZN-T1's 'unsubscribe rate must not exceed the other arm by more than 0.30pt' — at n=1,421 on a 0.5% base the 95% CI on that difference is about +/-0.52pt, so 0.30pt is inside noise.

issues.where: STAGES stage 2 successMetric — 'should beat the same cohort's Stage 3 ask by roughly 4-7 percentage points on opens'
issues.problem: Contradicted by the plan's own numbers on the next screen. Stage 2 is targeted at 18-24% and Stage 3 COLD at 16-22%: that is a 2pt gap at every point of the range, not 4-7pt.
issues.fix: Either raise Stage 3's target or state the real expectation: 'We expect the give to open roughly 2pt above the ask, which is inside the noise band at this list size and is not a number to celebrate or to act on.'

issues.where: STAGES stage 5 successMetric — '5b: 8-12% HUMAN open, which is roughly half to two-thirds of what the first email achieved on the same people'
issues.problem: 5b's audience is defined as people with no HUMAN open on Stage 2 or Stage 3. By construction the first email achieved 0% on these people, so 'half to two-thirds of what the first email achieved' is 0%. The follow-on rule ('anything above 12% means your first send's timing was wrong, not your list') is a made-up threshold resting on the same broken comparison.
issues.fix: Replace with: '5b is a recovery send to a cohort with a measured 0% HUMAN open. Any HUMAN open here is new information. We have no prior for what a retry recovers on this audience; the first run establishes it. Do not set a pass/fail threshold on the first observation.'

issues.where: STAGES stage 3 branch 'Registered' — 'a HUMAN click on the registration URL... measures intent and overstates completion by roughly 25-40%'
issues.problem: A precise-looking conversion-loss band for a quantity the same plan says has never been measured: GET /api/mailer/success 'records nothing today', there is no conversion_event table, and COHORTS B2 says 'the platform can prove the click and cannot prove the registration'. The click-to-registration ratio has therefore never been observed on this list or any prior edition.
issues.fix: 'Click-to-registration completion on a Zoom form is unknown for this audience. Reconcile the Zoom registrant CSV against the Stage 3 click set once, and that reconciliation becomes the first estimate. Do not forecast registrations from clicks until then.'

issues.where: STAGES stages 6a, 7c and 8a audience sizes
issues.problem: They do not reconcile to the list. Stage 6a claims ~1,450 non-registrants with at least one HUMAN open. Stage 7c claims 900-1,200 'engaged never-registered' — but 6a minus its own 60-100 registrations leaves ~1,350-1,390, not 900-1,200. Stage 8a claims 1,600-1,900 zero-engagement contacts. Adding 1,450 engaged + 1,750 silent + ~300 registrants = ~3,500 against a post-bounce mailable base of roughly 3,150-3,200, and against 3,023 if the holdout is honoured. The cohorts double-count by 300-500 people.
issues.fix: Rebuild these three numbers as a single subtraction from one mailable denominator and show the arithmetic: mailable = roster - undeliverable - holdout - bounces - unsubs; then registrants + engaged-unregistered + zero-engagement must sum to exactly that. Any figure that cannot be derived that way should not appear.

issues.where: A/B HZN-T0 primaryMetric and decisionRule
issues.problem: A validity problem, not just a power problem. Registration is measured by joining the Zoom export on lowercased email to the arm assignment CSV. Off-list arrivals — 191 of 209 June attendees by B15's own count — register with addresses that are not on the list and therefore cannot be matched to the holdout. The holdout's true organic registrations are systematically under-counted while the mailed arm's are matched, which biases the test toward finding a lift. The assumed organic rate p1 = 1.0% is itself unsourced and sits oddly against evidence that off-list channels dominated in June.
issues.fix: 'This holdout cannot measure organic registration, because organic registrants arrive with unmatched addresses by definition. Any lift it reports is an upper bound inflated by measurement asymmetry.' If you keep it, add a mandatory 'how did you hear about this' field to the Zoom form so holdout members are identifiable, or the test is not worth 340 people and ~20 foregone registrations.

issues.where: A/B HZN-T0 — baseline used three different ways
issues.problem: The sample-size math assumes mailed p2 = 5.0%; the guardrail costs the holdout at 'an expected 6% registration'; the observed June figure is 3.8%; the STAGES flow targets 7.3-9.9%. Four numbers for one quantity inside one plan, and the test's own text admits that at 3% it fails ('required n_small rises to roughly 470'). That 470 is also wrong — redoing it gives about 425 at p2=3%, and about 258 at the observed p2=3.8%.
issues.fix: Fix one baseline (3.8% observed) and propagate it everywhere. At p1=1%, p2=3.8%, 9:1 allocation, n_small = 258, so 340 does fit at the observed rate — but only if you also accept the measurement bias above. State the number once, in one place, and reference it.

issues.where: COHORTS exitRules — 'PERMANENT: domain-level burn. Five or more hard bounces or any complaint concentrated on one recipient domain means suppress the whole domain'
issues.problem: On a list that is 92.1% free-mail across 167 domains, roughly 3,100 addresses sit on a handful of domains led by gmail.com. Five hard bounces on gmail.com is a near-certainty in Stage 1 batch 1 alone, and 'any complaint' on gmail.com is close to guaranteed. Applied literally this rule suppresses the entire list on day one.
issues.fix: Add the exemption the rule is missing: 'Domain-level burn applies only to domains with fewer than 50 addresses on the list and a bounce rate above 20%. Free-mail providers (gmail, yahoo, rediffmail, hotmail, outlook) are exempt by definition and are managed by per-address suppression only.'

issues.where: STAGES stage 1 timing rationale ('07:10 is... the single highest-intent inbox moment for an Indian clinician'; '21:15 is after evening OPD') vs A/B HZN-T3
issues.problem: The calendar hard-codes 07:10 and 21:15 across the whole flow as if optimal, while HZN-T3 concludes that send-hour effects on a single-timezone list are 1-3pt, that detecting 2pt needs 8,390 per arm (5.0x the roster), and that the test 'cannot be won on this list in this edition, or in any single edition'. The plan simultaneously asserts the answer and proves it cannot know it. HZN-T3's 11:00 arm also violates the calendar's 'nothing sends between 11:00 and 16:00 IST'.
issues.fix: 'Send times are set by operational judgement, not evidence. We have no data on this audience's inbox behaviour and cannot acquire it at this list size. 07:10 and 21:15 are house defaults chosen for plausibility and consistency; they are not optimised and will not be tested.' Then either delete HZN-T3 or move its arms inside the permitted windows (e.g. 07:10 vs 20:00).

issues.where: STAGES stage 1 / calendar — warm-up ramp on the new horizonevent.info domain
issues.problem: The ramp is 230 / 170 / 400 / 600 / 1,100 / 860 across ten days on a domain with zero sending history, to a list that is 92% free-mail and substantially scraped. That is not a warm-up: it reaches 1,100 in a single send on day 8, and the ramp is non-monotonic (1,100 then 860). The claim that 'warm-up order is free cohort logic: doing it in engagement order costs nothing and buys deliverability' also fails because C1 and C2 are, per the evidence, 18 and <163 people, not 230 and 170.
issues.fix: Rebuild as a monotonic ramp with the real cohort sizes and stretch it: e.g. 50, 100, 200, 400, 700, 1,100, 1,300 across 14-18 days, each rung gated on the previous rung's bounce count. Add: 'A new domain sending 2,500+ cold scraped addresses inside ten days is the highest-risk element of this plan and is the most likely cause of a Stage 3 deliverability failure.'

issues.where: MEASUREMENT delivery-rate trap vs every A/B primary metric defined as X / delivered
issues.problem: The measurement doc states that 'delivered' is a subtraction using a bounce heuristic the code documents as over-counting whenever two campaigns mailed the same address inside the window, and that 'a 7-stage campaign at 3-4 day gaps triggers that condition on every stage after the first'. Every A/B test in the plan uses reliableOpens/delivered or reliableClicks/delivered as its primary metric, from Stage 2 onward — i.e. entirely inside the region where the denominator is known-wrong.
issues.fix: Set the denominator to sent (SES-accepted) for all arm comparisons and report delivered separately as a diagnostic. Add: 'Delivered-based rates are not comparable across stages in this flow because of a documented double-counting bug in bounce attribution; use sent as the denominator for anything you intend to compare.'

issues.where: STAGES stage 4 successMetric — '40-50% HUMAN open... Reply rate 3-6%, which is 15-27 real conversations. Registrations attributable to this stage 25-45'
issues.problem: Three unsupported numbers stacked. The open target breaches the classifier ceiling (see above). The reply band has no source and no prior — cold-to-warm reply rates of 3-6% are at the top of what a genuinely warm B2B list produces, and this cohort has already declined to register. The arithmetic is also off: 3% of 450 is 13.5, not 15. And 25-45 registrations from 450 people who already ignored three asks is 5.6-10.0%, which is higher than the whole flow's per-stage rate on cold audiences.
issues.fix: Replace with: 'No reply baseline exists. Plan for 1-3% (5-14 replies) and staff the 24h SLA for the top of that range. Attributable registrations: unknown; if 10-20 of 450 (2-4%) convert, the stage has paid for itself.' Publish the actual reply rate as the deliverable of this stage rather than a target to be hit.

issues.where: STAGES stage 6 successMetric — 'Attendance target 35-45% of registrants' and stage 6 branch 'the Horizon I benchmark of 80+ minutes average watch is the bar'
issues.problem: Both are stated as established figures with no source. Worse, the 35-45% band is contradicted by the plan's own June data, where 209 people attended against 163 registrants — a >100% attendance rate, which is only possible if the Zoom session did not require registration to join. If that is true, the entire B2/B3 registration-conversion architecture is measuring a gate that attendees can walk around, and 'never send the Zoom join link to a non-registrant' protects nothing.
issues.fix: First establish whether registration is actually required to join. Then: 'Free-webinar attendance on this audience is unmeasured. June produced 209 attendees against 163 registrants, which means registration was not a gate. Set no attendance target for Horizon IV; report registrant-to-attendee rate as a new baseline.' Drop the 80-minute Horizon I benchmark unless the dwell export can be produced.

issues.where: A/B HZN-T1 and HZN-T2 — arm sizes computed on the wrong roster
issues.problem: HZN-T1 says 'Actual SHA-256 mod 2 split on the real file gave 1,744 / 1,619' — those sum to 3,363, the full roster, not the 3,023 that remains after the holdout. HZN-T2's verified cross-tab '846 / 898 / 835 / 784' also sums to 3,363. So both splits were run on a file that includes the 340 people who are supposed to receive nothing, and the per-arm figures quoted downstream (1,421, 1,390) are not the arms that will actually be mailed. The 1,744/1,619 imbalance is also 2.15 sigma from an even hash split, which is unusual enough (p≈0.03) to be worth re-checking the hashing code rather than accepting.
issues.fix: Re-run both splits on the post-holdout, post-verification file and requote every per-arm n. While re-running, verify the hash is a true uniform parity (int(sha256_hex, 16) % 2), not parity of a single character position, and confirm the imbalance persists.

issues.where: A/B HZN-T6 decisionRule — 'run the reply CTA UNTESTED to the whole non-registrant slice at Stage 4, since the brief already believes in it and an untested tactic beats a test you cannot measure'
issues.problem: This converts an unmeasurable test into an unmeasurable full rollout to ~2,550 people, at the exact stage where variant B removes the registration link entirely. If the reply CTA underperforms, you have deleted the only measurable conversion path from the final reminder and will never know what it cost. 'An untested tactic beats a test you cannot measure' is not a principle; it is a way of never being wrong.
issues.fix: Keep the link in every arm. 'Run the reply CTA as an addition to the registration link, never as a replacement, on at most 20-30% of the non-registrant slice. Compare that slice's registration rate to the rest via the Zoom export. That is a crude read but it is not zero, and it costs nothing.'

issues.where: COHORTS exitRules — 'PERMANENT: verification verdict UNDELIVERABLE... this exit is enforced without any marketer action'
issues.problem: queueFromList can only exclude addresses that have a verification_result row. The pre-flight runs POST /api/verification/list on C4 only. C1, C2 and C3 are never verified, so for roughly 800 addresses this 'automatic' exit is inert. The rule reads as platform-enforced coverage of the whole list when it covers one cohort.
issues.fix: 'Verification exclusion is automatic only for addresses that have been verified. Verify all four cohorts pre-flight, or state that C1-C3 ship unverified and accept the corresponding bounce risk on the warmest, most reputation-sensitive first sends.'

issues.where: STAGES stage 2 audience — 'approximately 3,290'
issues.problem: 3,363 minus 3,290 is 73, i.e. the plan assumes about 2% total attrition after the entire list has been touched once on a brand-new domain. Its own gates allow batch 1 bounce up to 4% and unsubscribe 0.3-0.8%, and the MEASUREMENT doc estimates Stage 1 delivery at 94-97% (3-6% bounce). Pre-flight verification will remove more before Stage 1 even fires. This is a quiet assumption that the list is cleaner than the plan elsewhere says it is.
issues.fix: Recompute: 3,363 - ~5% undeliverable (168) - 340 holdout - ~4% bounce (121) - ~0.5% unsub (15) = roughly 2,720 mailable at Stage 2, not 3,290. Carry that number through Stages 3-8, which currently all inherit the optimistic base.

issues.where: STAGES stage 3 successMetric — 'the June run had 163 registrants on the board at send time against 3,367 emailed, about 3.8%'
issues.problem: 163/3,367 = 4.84%, not 3.8%. The 3.8% comes from HZN-T6's separate and different figure of 128 registered at send time. The sentence fuses the larger numerator with the smaller ratio, and then uses it to claim 'a good single ask email roughly matches what the entire previous two-email campaign produced'.
issues.fix: Pick one: '128 of 3,367 emailed (3.8%) were registered at Stage 3 send time' or '163 total registrants (4.8% of emailed), of whom 35 were off-list'. Do not mix them, and drop the 'roughly matches' comparison until the reconciliation in issue 1 is done.

issues.where: List size: 3,363 (A/B, cohorts) vs 3,367 emailed (stage 3, HZN-T6); free-mail 92.1% (A/B) vs 88% (stage 1 successMetric, stage 5 teachingNote) vs 92% (COHORTS B8, fatigue exit)
issues.problem: Two different list sizes and two different free-mail percentages circulate through documents that are meant to be operationally precise. The 88% figure is used specifically to justify deliverability targets and the one-retry rule, so it is load-bearing.
issues.fix: State once: 'horizon-clean.csv, 18 Aug 2026, 3,363 rows, 3,363 unique emails, 92.1% free-mail, 167 domains, recomputed from the file.' The 3,367 is the June Postmark send count and belongs only in sentences about June. Replace every '88%' with 92.1%.

issues.where: COHORTS exitRules FREQUENCY-CAP PARK — 'more than three sends to one address in any rolling seven days' vs its own SQL 'HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3' and STAGES stage 2/5 killCriteria 'received three emails in the previous seven days'
issues.problem: The prose sets the cap at four or more; the SQL and both killCriteria set it at three or more. These produce different parked sets on every stage, and the rule is described as a manual pre-send step, so the discrepancy will be resolved differently by whoever runs it that day.
issues.fix: Pick >= 3 (the stricter, and what the SQL already does) and make the prose match: 'Three or more sends to one address inside a rolling seven days parks that address for the next stage.'

issues.where: A/B HZN-T3 decisionRule — 'after 6 stages x 3 editions (pooled 8,400 person-stages per arm)'
issues.problem: 6 stages x 3 editions x 1,400 = 25,200 person-stages per arm, not 8,400 (8,400 is one edition). The test is otherwise the most honest in the set, and it correctly notes that person-stages are not independent samples, so the error is cosmetic but sits inside the one paragraph a reader will trust.
issues.fix: 'Pooled 25,200 person-stages per arm across three editions, but still only 1,400 distinct people per arm — the repeated observations do not add independent information, which is why this stays exploratory forever.'

issues.where: A/B HZN-T2 decisionRule fallback — 'switch the primary to click rate on the registration link (base approx 3%, CI on a difference is +/-1.26pt at this n, so a 2pt click gap IS readable)'
issues.problem: The +/-1.26pt is arithmetically correct, but the framing is misleading. A 2pt gap on a 3% base is 3% vs 5%, a 67% relative swing in clicks caused by a subject line. That will not happen, so the fallback metric is 'readable' only in the sense that it will read null every time. Also, Stage 2 in the STAGES doc has no registration link at all (it is the no-ask give), so the fallback metric may not exist for that stage.
issues.fix: 'Falling back to clicks does not rescue this test: the click MDE at this n is about 2pt on a 3% base, which is a 67% relative effect that a subject line will not produce. Report the open difference with its CI, label it directional, and pool across editions. Also confirm the stage actually contains a registration link before nominating click rate as its primary metric.'

issues.where: COHORTS B10 — 'if they concentrate in one pre-send cohort (P6 cold pipeline addresses is the prime suspect)'
issues.problem: The cohort model supplied defines B1-B15 only. There is no P-series anywhere in these documents, and no provenance or source field is described on subscriber or on horizon-clean.csv. A suppression decision ('the fix is to stop mailing it') is keyed to a segment that may not be constructible.
issues.fix: Either publish the P-series definition and the provenance column it depends on, or rewrite as: 'If complaints concentrate, we currently cannot attribute them to a source cohort because horizon-clean.csv carries no provenance field. Adding a source column at import is a prerequisite for acting on complaint concentration at all.'

issues.where: STAGES stage 6 successMetric and stage 7 timing — 'Last chance is reliably the second-largest registration driver in a flow like this after the first ask'; 'the certificate is the single highest-click asset in the entire flow'
issues.problem: Two confident benchmarks with no source, no prior edition data cited, and no mechanism by which this organisation could have observed either (there is no conversion tracking and no per-link labelling until distinct URLs are introduced by this very plan).
issues.fix: Mark both as priors: 'In published webinar flows the last-chance send is commonly the second-largest registration driver; we have no Horizon data confirming this and Horizon IV will be the first edition that can measure it.' Same for the certificate claim.

issues.where: A/B HZN-T2 variantA subject line — 'Horizon Series, 27 Sept'
issues.problem: The STAGES calendar places the event on Saturday 26 Sep 2026, with 27 Sep as E+1. The tested subject line advertises the wrong date, which would both mislead recipients and confound the test with a copy defect.
issues.fix: Correct to 26 Sept, and add a pre-send check to the runbook that every date string in every arm matches the canonical stage table.
